Kind = Literal["change", "preserve", "no_vehicle_change"]
_STATUS_RANK = {"standard": 0, "optional": 1, "no_cost_option": 1, "not_available": 2}


class Profile(_Strict):
    requirement: str
    kind: Kind = "change"
    changes: list[Change] = []
    note: str | None = None

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check(self) -> Profile:
        if self.kind == "change" and not self.changes:
            raise ValueError(f"{self.requirement}: kind 'change' needs at least one change")
        if self.kind != "change" and (self.changes or not self.note):
            raise ValueError(f"{self.requirement}: kind '{self.kind}' takes a note and no changes")
        return self


class ProfileFile(_Strict):
    vehicle: str
    market: str
    author: str
    profiles: list[Profile] = Field(min_length=1)


def portfolio_scan(session: Session, vehicle: str, terms: list[str]) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """Best catalogue status per vehicle for items whose name matches one of the terms, and the
    portfolio level: 0 standard on this vehicle, 1 optional on this vehicle, 2 offered on another
    BMW series (carry over), 3 not in any catalogue (new for BMW)."""
    if not terms:
        return None
    match = or_(
        *[
            EquipmentItem.name_de.ilike(f"%{t}%") | EquipmentItem.name_en.ilike(f"%{t}%")
            for t in terms
        ]
    )
    rows = session.execute(
        select(
        },
    }


def _portfolio_flags(c: Change, scan: dict[str, Any] | None, vehicle: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    if scan is None:
        return []
    found = ", ".join(f"{v} {x['status']}" for v, x in scan["vehicles"].items()) or "nothing"
    own = scan["own_variants"]
    spread = (
        f"standard on {own['standard']}, optional on {own['optional']} of {own['total']} "
        f"{vehicle} variants"
    )
    if scan["level"] == 2 and not c.carryover:
        return [
            _flag(
                "warning",
                "43",
                f"{c.subsystem}: catalogue shows {found}; the change could carry over "
                "(carryover: true) instead of a new development",
            )
        ]
    if scan["level"] == 3 and c.carryover:
        return [
            _flag(
                "warning",
                "43",
                f"{c.subsystem}: carryover is claimed but no catalogue item matches "
                f"{scan['terms']}; cite the source of the carryover",
            )
        ]
    if scan["level"] in (0, 1) and c.layer != "K0":
        status = "standard" if scan["level"] == 0 else "optional"
        return [
            _flag(
                "info",
                "43",
                f"{c.subsystem}: already {status} on {vehicle} ({spread}); check whether only "
                "configuration (K0) is needed",
            )
        ]
    return []


def _flag(level: str, rule: str, text: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    return {"level": level, "rule": rule, "text": text}


def horizon_flags(horizon: str, kind: str, decision: str, stable: float) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """Rules 47 / 48 / 51: does the estimated class fit the requirement's horizon?"""
    out = []
    if kind != "change":
        return out
    if horizon == "H1" and decision == "new generation":
        out.append(
            _flag(
                "conflict",
                "47",
                "H1 but the estimate needs a new generation; move to H2 (successor) or split",
            )
        )
    elif horizon == "H1" and decision == "major revision":
        out.append(
            _flag("warning", "47", "H1 but the estimate is beyond a normal LCI (major revision)")
        )
    elif horizon == "H2" and decision == "adapt":
        out.append(
            _flag(
                "info",
                "48",
                "H2 but the estimate fits a life-cycle impulse; could be pulled forward to H1",
            )
        )
    if stable < 90:
        out.append(
            _flag(
                "warning",
                "51",
                f"borderline: only {stable:.0f} % of the sensitivity runs keep the decision; "
                "show the PM both options",
            )
        )
    return out


# ---- estimate run -------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _content(e: RequirementEffort) -> dict[str, Any]:
    keys = (
        "requirement_version",
        "kind",
        "effort_pct",
        "p5",
        "p95",
        "decision",
        "decision_stable_pct",
        "layer",
        "size",
        "certification",
        "changes",
        "subsystems",
        "portfolio",
        "flags",
        "note",
        "model_hash",
    )
    return {k: getattr(e, k) for k in keys}


class _Engines:
def estimate_all(
    session: Session,
    run: Run,
    *,
    directory: Path | None = None,
    runs: int = 2000,
    scope: JitterScope = "all",
    seed: int = 42,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    cfg = load_model()
    mhash = model_hash(cfg)
    engines = _Engines(cfg, runs, scope, seed)
    files = load_profiles(directory)
    stats: dict[str, Any] = {"created": 0, "updated": 0, "unchanged": 0, "model_hash": mhash}

    errors: list[str] = []
    seen: set[str] = set()
    plan: list[tuple[ProfileFile, Profile, Requirement]] = []
    for f in files:
        engine, _ = engines.get(f.vehicle)
        for p in f.profiles:
            if p.requirement in seen:
                errors.append(f"duplicate profile {p.requirement}")
            seen.add(p.requirement)
            req = session.get(Requirement, p.requirement)
            if req is None or req.status == "withdrawn":
                errors.append(f"{p.requirement}: unknown or withdrawn requirement")
                continue
            if (req.vehicle_code, req.market_code) != (f.vehicle, f.market):
                errors.append(f"{p.requirement}: belongs to {req.vehicle_code} {req.market_code}")
            errors += [f"{p.requirement}: {e}" for c in p.changes for e in engine.check_change(c)]
            plan.append((f, p, req))
    if errors:
        raise ValueError("effort profiles: " + "; ".join(errors))

    active = session.scalars(select(Requirement).where(Requirement.status != "withdrawn")).all()
    stats["missing_profiles"] = sorted(r.id for r in active if r.id not in seen)

    for f, p, req in plan:
        engine, samples = engines.get(f.vehicle)
        res = evaluate(engine, samples, p.changes, p.kind)
        scans = []
        flags: list[dict[str, str]] = []
        for c in p.changes:
            scan = portfolio_scan(session, f.vehicle, c.portfolio_terms)
            if scan:
                scans.append({"subsystem": c.subsystem, **scan})
            flags += _portfolio_flags(c, scan, f.vehicle)
        flags += horizon_flags(req.horizon, p.kind, res["decision"], res["decision_stable_pct"])
        values = {
            "requirement_version": req.version,
            "kind": p.kind,
            "effort_pct": res["effort_pct"],
            "p5": res["p5"],
            "p95": res["p95"],
            "decision": res["decision"],
            "decision_stable_pct": res["decision_stable_pct"],
            "layer": res["layer"],
            "size": res["size"],
            "certification": res["certification_add_on"],
            "changes": [c.model_dump() for c in p.changes],
            "subsystems": res["subsystems"],
            "portfolio": scans,
            "flags": flags,
            "note": p.note,
            "model_hash": mhash,
        }
        row = session.get(RequirementEffort, req.id)
        if row is None:
            row = RequirementEffort(requirement_id=req.id, created_run_id=run.id, **values)
            session.add(row)
            action, before = "effort.estimated", None
            stats["created"] += 1
        else:
            before = _content(row)
            for k, v in values.items():
                setattr(row, k, v)
            if _content(row) == before:
                stats["unchanged"] += 1
                continue
            action = "effort.updated"
            stats["updated"] += 1
        row.updated_run_id = run.id
        session.flush()
        record_event(
            session,
            actor_type="system",
            actor_id="effort-engine",
            action=action,
            entity_type="requirement",

def _portfolio_flags(c: Change, scan: dict[str, Any] | None, vehicle: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    if scan is None:
        return []
    found = ", ".join(f"{v} {x['status']}" for v, x in scan["vehicles"].items()) or "nothing"
    own = scan["own_variants"]
    spread = (
        f"standard on {own['standard']}, optional on {own['optional']} of {own['total']} "
        f"{vehicle} variants"
    )
    if scan["level"] == 2 and not c.carryover:
        return [
            _flag(
                "warning",
                "43",
                f"{c.subsystem}: catalogue shows {found}; the change could carry over "
                "(carryover: true) instead of a new development",
            )
        ]
    if scan["level"] == 3 and c.carryover:
        return [
            _flag(
                "warning",
                "43",
                f"{c.subsystem}: carryover is claimed but no catalogue item matches "
                f"{scan['terms']}; cite the source of the carryover",
            )
        ]
    if scan["level"] in (0, 1) and c.layer != "K0":
        status = "standard" if scan["level"] == 0 else "optional"
        return [
            _flag(
                "info",
                "43",
                f"{c.subsystem}: already {status} on {vehicle} ({spread}); check whether only "
                "configuration (K0) is needed",
            )
        ]
    return []


def _flag(level: str, rule: str, text: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    return {"level": level, "rule": rule, "text": text}


def horizon_flags(horizon: str, kind: str, decision: str, stable: float) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """Rules 47 / 48 / 51: does the estimated class fit the requirement's horizon?"""
    out = []
    if kind != "change":
        return out
    if horizon == "H1" and decision == "new generation":
        out.append(
            _flag(
                "conflict",
                "47",
                "H1 but the estimate needs a new generation; move to H2 (successor) or split",
            )
        )
    elif horizon == "H1" and decision == "major revision":
        out.append(
            _flag("warning", "47", "H1 but the estimate is beyond a normal LCI (major revision)")
        )
    elif horizon == "H2" and decision == "adapt":
        out.append(
            _flag(
                "info",
                "48",
                "H2 but the estimate fits a life-cycle impulse; could be pulled forward to H1",
            )
        )
    if stable < 90:
        out.append(
            _flag(
                "warning",
                "51",
                f"borderline: only {stable:.0f} % of the sensitivity runs keep the decision; "
                "show the PM both options",
            )
        )
    return out

class _Engines:
def estimate_all(
    session: Session,
    run: Run,
    *,
    directory: Path | None = None,
    runs: int = 2000,
    scope: JitterScope = "all",
    seed: int = 42,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    cfg = load_model()
    mhash = model_hash(cfg)
    engines = _Engines(cfg, runs, scope, seed)
    files = load_profiles(directory)
    stats: dict[str, Any] = {"created": 0, "updated": 0, "unchanged": 0, "model_hash": mhash}

    errors: list[str] = []
    seen: set[str] = set()
    plan: list[tuple[ProfileFile, Profile, Requirement]] = []
    for f in files:
        engine, _ = engines.get(f.vehicle)
        for p in f.profiles:
            if p.requirement in seen:
                errors.append(f"duplicate profile {p.requirement}")
            seen.add(p.requirement)
            req = session.get(Requirement, p.requirement)
            if req is None or req.status == "withdrawn":
                errors.append(f"{p.requirement}: unknown or withdrawn requirement")
                continue
            if (req.vehicle_code, req.market_code) != (f.vehicle, f.market):
                errors.append(f"{p.requirement}: belongs to {req.vehicle_code} {req.market_code}")
            errors += [f"{p.requirement}: {e}" for c in p.changes for e in engine.check_change(c)]
            plan.append((f, p, req))
    if errors:
        raise ValueError("effort profiles: " + "; ".join(errors))

    active = session.scalars(select(Requirement).where(Requirement.status != "withdrawn")).all()
    stats["missing_profiles"] = sorted(r.id for r in active if r.id not in seen)

    for f, p, req in plan:
        engine, samples = engines.get(f.vehicle)
        res = evaluate(engine, samples, p.changes, p.kind)
        scans = []
        flags: list[dict[str, str]] = []
        for c in p.changes:
            scan = portfolio_scan(session, f.vehicle, c.portfolio_terms)
            if scan:
                scans.append({"subsystem": c.subsystem, **scan})
            flags += _portfolio_flags(c, scan, f.vehicle)
        flags += horizon_flags(req.horizon, p.kind, res["decision"], res["decision_stable_pct"])
        values = {
            "requirement_version": req.version,
            "kind": p.kind,
            "effort_pct": res["effort_pct"],
            "p5": res["p5"],
            "p95": res["p95"],
            "decision": res["decision"],
            "decision_stable_pct": res["decision_stable_pct"],
            "layer": res["layer"],
            "size": res["size"],
            "certification": res["certification_add_on"],
            "changes": [c.model_dump() for c in p.changes],
            "subsystems": res["subsystems"],
            "portfolio": scans,
            "flags": flags,
            "note": p.note,
            "model_hash": mhash,
        }
        row = session.get(RequirementEffort, req.id)
        if row is None:
            row = RequirementEffort(requirement_id=req.id, created_run_id=run.id, **values)
            session.add(row)
            action, before = "effort.estimated", None
            stats["created"] += 1
        else:
            before = _content(row)
            for k, v in values.items():
                setattr(row, k, v)
            if _content(row) == before:
                stats["unchanged"] += 1
                continue
            action = "effort.updated"
            stats["updated"] += 1
        row.updated_run_id = run.id
        session.flush()
        record_event(
            session,
            actor_type="system",
            actor_id="effort-engine",
            action=action,
            entity_type="requirement",
            entity_id=req.id,
            run_id=run.id,
            before=before,
            after=_content(row),
            rationale=f"CPM effort model {mhash}, profile by {f.author}",
        )
    stats["flags"] = {
        level: sum(
            1
            for row in session.scalars(select(RequirementEffort))
            for fl in row.flags
            if fl["level"] == level
        )
        for level in ("conflict", "warning", "info")
    }
    return stats

# Back-test anchors: publicly documented BMW decisions, classified by the same engine and inputs
# (`tracepoint effort backtest`). `changes` are authored like requirement change profiles.
# `independent: false` marks an anchor that repeats the inputs of another one, so it is not an
# independent test (the iX3 LWB uses the same inputs as the G68).
anchors:
  - id: g30-lci-colours-wheels
    name: New colors/wheels (G30 LCI 2020)
    changes: [{subsystem: paint_color, own_impact: 0.5, layer: K1, why: "New paint shades and wheel designs on existing interfaces"}]
    actual: adapt
    evidence: Delivered with the G30 facelift 2020
    source: https://www.bmwblog.com/2020/05/26/bmw-5-series-facelift
  - id: g30-lci-lights-bumper
    name: New headlights + front bumper (G30 LCI)
    changes: [{subsystem: exterior_design, own_impact: 0.5, layer: K2, why: "New headlight units and front bumper on the same body"}]
    actual: adapt
    evidence: Delivered with the G30 facelift 2020
    source: https://www.bmwblog.com/2020/05/26/bmw-5-series-facelift
  - id: g30-lci-os7
    name: New software OS 7 + OTA (G30 LCI 2020)
    changes: [{subsystem: software_hmi, own_impact: 0.4, layer: K2, why: "New operating system release with over-the-air capability"}]
    actual: adapt
    evidence: Delivered with the G30 facelift 2020
    source: https://www.bmwblog.com/2020/05/26/bmw-5-series-facelift
  - id: g30-lci-545e
    name: New PHEV 545e from module kit (G30 LCI)
    changes: [{subsystem: powertrain, own_impact: 0.4, layer: K2, carryover: true, why: "Plug-in hybrid drive taken from the modular kit already used on CLAR"}]
    actual: adapt
    evidence: Delivered with the G30 facelift 2020
    source: https://www.bmwblog.com/2020/05/26/bmw-5-series-facelift
  - id: g68-lwb
    name: Long wheelbase G68 China (at launch)
    changes:
      - subsystem: body_structure
        own_impact: 0.4
        layer: K2
        why: >-
          Stretched body on the same platform, developed in parallel with the G60. Rule 42 lists
          the wheelbase as K3; here the platform is prepared for it and the body is not replaced
          (40 %), so it is a K2 module change. See the note in reports/step-12-cpm-effort-engine.md.
    actual: major revision
certification:
  add_on: 12
  trigger_subsystems: [body_structure, hv_battery, powertrain]
  min_own_impact: 0.3

# Rule 43: multiplier on the first-hop likelihoods when the feature already exists in the
# portfolio or the platform was prepared for it (interfaces already designed).
carryover_factor: 0.3

# The link likelihoods describe a change of the usual size of a module change (own impact about
# 0.3, the smallest anchor of the back-test). A smaller change propagates proportionally less:
# its first-hop likelihoods are scaled by own_impact / 0.3. Without this, a 3 % calibration
# propagates as far as a redesign (found when the requirement profiles were first estimated).
propagation_reference_impact: 0.3

# Rules 42 / 47: replacing a platform subsystem (almost) completely without carryover is a K3
# change and means a new generation regardless of the score. A change that matches this rule
# must be authored as K3; the import refuses anything lower.
platform_rule:
  subsystems: [body_structure, hv_battery, powertrain, ee_architecture]
  min_own_impact: 0.8

# Rule 47 thresholds in % of a new vehicle (PM-editable).
thresholds: {major_revision: 15, new_generation: 50}

# K0 (configuration: standard content, package, OTA activation of existing hardware) does not
# propagate; its own impact must stay small.
k0_max_own_impact: 0.1

max_path_length: 3

# T-shirt sizes for the PM workspace (upper bound, exclusive); everything above L is XL.
sizes: {XS: 1, S: 5, M: 15, L: 50}

# Per-vehicle applicability. Subsystems listed as absent are removed and the weights renormalised
# to 100 for that vehicle; a change that starts in an absent subsystem is refused (it would be a
# new powertrain concept for that car, i.e. a new generation).

"""Situation analysis of one vehicle in one market or country, written by the analyst agent.

The agent starts from the context pack, drills down with the tools and answers in a fixed schema
in which every insight and recommendation cites its evidence. The analysis is a proposal for the
product manager: it reads the evidence store and changes nothing in it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from typing import Any, Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from tracepoint.agent.context_pack import build_context_pack, render_markdown
from tracepoint.agent.loop import collect_refs, run_agent
from tracepoint.core.audit import record_event
from tracepoint.db.models import Country, Run, Verbatim
from tracepoint.llm.gateway import LlmGateway

PROMPT_VERSION = "situation-analysis-v2"  # v2: the loop's untrusted-data rule joins the prompt
ACTOR = "agent:analyst"


class Insight(BaseModel):
    title: str
    kind: Literal[
        "recurring_complaint", "unmet_need", "strength", "metric_gap", "equipment_gap", "context"
    ]
    domain: str = Field(description="Vehicle domain key as written in the context pack")
    statement: str = Field(description="What the evidence shows, with its numbers")
    customer_quote: str | None = Field(description="One short verbatim quote, or null")
    evidence_refs: list[str] = Field(min_length=1)
    confidence: Literal["high", "medium", "low"]


class Recommendation(BaseModel):
    title: str
    proposal: str = Field(description="What the product manager should consider, customer-facing")
    horizon: Literal["H1", "H2"]
    rationale: str
    evidence_refs: list[str] = Field(min_length=1)
    related_requirement: str | None = Field(
        description="Id of an existing requirement (REQ-…) that already covers this, or null"
    )


class SituationAnalysis(BaseModel):
    headline: str
    summary: str
    data_coverage: str = Field(description="Which evidence the analysis rests on and how much")
    insights: list[Insight]
    recommendations: list[Recommendation]
    assumptions_and_gaps: list[str]


SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are the situation analyst of Tracepoint, a customer-requirements workbench for BMW product managers. You analyse one BMW model in one market, or in one country of that market, from the stored evidence. You report what customers experience, what they miss, what has to be kept, and what the product manager should look at first.

How to work
1. The user message holds the context pack of the scope. Read it first.
2. Drill down with the tools before you conclude. Read the verbatims behind the largest complaint themes and behind the strengths (get_verbatims_by_theme, search_evidence). Check the study metrics (get_metric), the catalogue (get_equipment), the sales weight (get_sales), the extracted findings (get_findings) and the requirements already derived (get_requirements). Ask for the requirements without a status filter: most are still proposed and wait for the product manager's decision. Use search_documents for the BMW Group's strategy and delivery figures.
3. Search is lexical: when a query returns little, try the customers' other words for the same thing.
4. Stop calling tools once another call would not change the analysis. Then answer in the JSON schema.

Evidence rules
- Every insight and every recommendation lists the references it rests on in evidence_refs, copied exactly as you received them: evidence_ref values (verbatim:…, metric:…, equipment:…, sales:…, document:…) and the ids of findings and requirements (FND-…, REQ-…). A reference you were not given is rejected.
- Every number comes from the context pack or from a tool result. Use no figure from memory and no knowledge about competitors or markets that is not in the evidence.
- A customer quote is copied word for word from a verbatim you cite, and kept short.

        f"country {country} (market {market})" if country else f"market {market}"
    )

            if country

        )

    )

    out = {

        "vehicle": vehicle,
        "market": market,
        "country": country,
        "scope": scope,
        "prompt_version": PROMPT_VERSION,

        "model": result.model,
        "analysis": result.parsed.model_dump(),

            "unverified_quotes": quotes,
        },
        "trace": {
            "steps": result.steps,
            "cached_steps": result.cached_steps,
            "hit_step_limit": result.hit_step_limit,

def render_analysis(out: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    a, trace = out["analysis"], out["trace"]
    unknown = set(out["citations"]["unknown"])
    loose_quotes = set(out["citations"]["unverified_quotes"])

    def refs(items: list[str]) -> str:
        return ", ".join(f"`{r}`" + (" (not verified)" if r in unknown else "") for r in items)

    lines = [
        f"# Situation analysis – {out['scope']}",
        "",
        f"Run `{out['run_id']}` · {out['model']} · {out['prompt_version']} · "
        f"{trace['steps']} steps, {len(trace['tool_calls'])} tool calls · "
        f"{out['citations']['cited']} references cited, {len(unknown)} not verified · "
        f"{len(loose_quotes)} quotes not found in their verbatims",
        "",
        f"**{a['headline']}**",
        "",
        a["summary"],
        "",
        "## Data coverage",
        a["data_coverage"],
        "",
        "## Insights",
    ]
    for i in a["insights"]:
        lines += [
            "",
            f"### {i['title']}",
            f"{i['kind']} · {i['domain']} · confidence {i['confidence']}",
            "",
            i["statement"],
        ]
        if i["customer_quote"]:
            flag = " (not found word for word in the cited verbatims)"
            lines += [
                "",
                f"> {i['customer_quote']}" + (flag if i["customer_quote"] in loose_quotes else ""),
            ]
        lines += ["", f"Evidence: {refs(i['evidence_refs'])}"]
    lines += ["", "## Recommendations (proposals for the product manager)"]
    for r in a["recommendations"]:
        lines += ["", f"### {r['title']} ({r['horizon']})", r["proposal"], "", r["rationale"]]
        if r["related_requirement"]:
            lines += ["", f"Existing requirement: {refs([r['related_requirement']])}"]
        lines += ["", f"Evidence: {refs(r['evidence_refs'])}"]
    lines += ["", "## Assumptions and gaps"] + [f"- {x}" for x in a["assumptions_and_gaps"]]
    lines += ["", "## Tool calls"]
    lines += [
        f"- `{c['tool']}` {c['args']} → " + (c["error"] if "error" in c else f"{c.get('total')}")
        for c in trace["tool_calls"]
    ]
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

**Step 13 – BMW Group Report.** `docs/BMW-Group-Report-2025-en.pdf` was in `docs/` but no parser read it. It is now the ninth internal source: one `document_page` row per page (434), columns read in order, searchable through the agent tool `search_documents` (D-065).

**Step 14 – agent loop and situation analyst.**
- The LLM gateway carries conversation history and tool calls. Caching, call logging and the cost caps work as before.
- `agent/loop.py` runs a model against the drill-down tools until it answers in a schema. An answer may cite only references the agent was given; unknown references and quotes not found in their verbatims go back once for correction and are reported if they survive (D-066).

- A country narrows the customer verbatims; studies, sales and findings stay per market. Findings are extracted for all ten scopes (D-068).

**Step 15 – CPM effort in the analysis (D-071).** Merged `main` (PR #16, effort engine). The analyst never writes an effort figure: a proposal takes the stored change profile of the requirement it names, or carries a change profile of its own, and the CPM engine computes effort, P5–P95, class and size per proposal and per H1 / H2 package. A profile that breaks the model, or a proposal whose class does not fit its horizon, goes back to the model once.

**Security review fixes (D-069, D-070).** The quote check no longer passes quotes it cannot compare. Tool results are marked as data in every agent's system prompt. A cost cap over 24 hours spans runs, refuses unpriced models and counts every billed answer; the endpoint runs one analysis at a time.

Also in this branch: server-side actor for G2 decisions and JSON-only write bodies (`031ca27`), and the gateway fixes for an empty base URL and dated model snapshots.

Main's decisions D-062 to D-064 and its step 12 report were already published. This branch's decisions moved to D-065 to D-071 and its reports to steps 13, 14 and 15. Commit messages before the merge still carry the old numbers.

- A repeat run on unchanged data is served from the cache at no cost.
- Samples: `reports/analysis/G60_US.md`, `reports/analysis/F70_GB.md` (prompt v3).

## For the reviewer

- New setting `TRACEPOINT_LLM_MAX_COST_USD_PER_DAY` (default 50) applies to every LLM job, bulk classification included. A model without a price in `config/llm/pricing.yaml` is refused while a cap is set.
- `POST /agent/analyze` spends tokens and has no authentication (D-014). The API must stay bound to localhost.
- `search_documents` sends passages of the Group Report to the LLM provider. The PDF metadata carries a "CONFIDENTIAL" template marking; please confirm the file may be sent.
- The analyst's own change profiles are assumptions on an uncalibrated effort model and live in the analysis file only.
- A database built before this branch needs `./start.sh`, or `tracepoint db init`, `ingest documents` and `effort estimate`.

Reports: `reports/step-13-group-report-ingestion.md`, `reports/step-14-analyst-agent-loop.md`, `reports/step-15-cpm-effort-in-the-analysis.md`.

Also in this branch: server-side actor for G2 decisions and JSON-only write bodies (`031ca27`), and the gateway fixes for an empty base URL and dated model snapshots.

## Renumbering after the merge

Main's decisions D-062 to D-064 and its step 12 report were already published. This branch's decisions moved to D-065 to D-071 and its reports to steps 13, 14 and 15. Commit messages before the merge still carry the old numbers.

## Verified

- 62 tests pass; `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean.
- Live analyses with `gpt-5.4`: G60 US, G60 KR and F70 GB with prompt v3 (effort included); every cited reference and quote verified. Effort of proposals that name a requirement equals `reports/effort/`.
- A repeat run on unchanged data is served from the cache at no cost.
- Samples: `reports/analysis/G60_US.md`, `reports/analysis/F70_GB.md` (prompt v3).

## For the reviewer

- New setting `TRACEPOINT_LLM_MAX_COST_USD_PER_DAY` (default 50) applies to every LLM job, bulk classification included. A model without a price in `config/llm/pricing.yaml` is refused while a cap is set.
- `POST /agent/analyze` spends tokens and has no authentication (D-014). The API must stay bound to localhost.
- `search_documents` sends passages of the Group Report to the LLM provider. The PDF metadata carries a "CONFIDENTIAL" template marking; please confirm the file may be sent.
- The analyst's own change profiles are assumptions on an uncalibrated effort model and live in the analysis file only.
- A database built before this branch needs `./start.sh`, or `tracepoint db init`, `ingest documents` and `effort estimate`.

Reports: `reports/step-13-group-report-ingestion.md`, `reports/step-14-analyst-agent-loop.md`, `reports/step-15-cpm-effort-in-the-analysis.md`.

Main merge edildi ve CPM analiz sürecine bağlandı. Testler 62 passed, lint temiz; commit atıldı, push edildi (`fef9cf9`), PR #15 güncellendi ve `main` ile çakışmasız.

## Merge
- Üç dosyada çakışma vardı (`api/app.py`, `cli.py`, `plan/decisions.md`); iki taraf da korundu.
- **Yeniden numaralandırma:** main'in D-062–D-064 kararları ve step 12 raporu zaten yayındaydı. Benim kararlarım D-065–D-071'e, raporlarım step 13 (Group Report), step 14 (agent loop) ve step 15'e (CPM) kaydı.

## CPM entegrasyonu nasıl çalışıyor
- **Model effort rakamı yazmıyor.** Her öneri için rakamı CPM motoru hesaplıyor.
- **İki kaynak:**
  - Öneri mevcut bir requirement'a bağlıysa o requirement'ın kayıtlı change profile'ı kullanılıyor.
  - Bağlı değilse agent kendi change profile'ını yazıyor (subsystem, own impact, layer, carryover) ve raporda "analyst's change profile" diye işaretleniyor.
- **Öneri başına:** effort %, P5–P95, sınıf (adapt / major revision / new generation), size, layer, flag'ler.
- **Paket başına:** H1 ve H2 önerileri subsystem bazında birleştiriliyor; ortak iş bir kez sayılıyor.
- **Düzeltme turu:** modeli bozan profile ya da horizon'una uymayan öneri (ör. H1 ama new generation) hesaplanan rakamla modele geri gidiyor.
- **Prompt:** effort'un para olmadığı, kalibre edilmemiş varsayım olduğu ve müşteri ihtiyacından sonra geldiği yazılı. Aracın effort modeli `config/effort/`'tan okunup mesaja ekleniyor.

## Canlı sonuçlar (`gpt-5.4`, prompt v3)

| Kapsam | Öneri | Profil kaynağı | H1 paketi | H2 paketi | Maliyet (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| G60, pazar US | 8 | 8 requirement | 13,1 %, adapt (koşuların % 69'unda) | 49,0 %, new generation | 0,19 |
| G60, ülke KR | 5 | 4 analist, 1 değişiklik yok | 7,5 %, adapt | 12,4 %, adapt | 0,14 |
| F70, ülke GB | 8 | 8 requirement | 10,4 %, adapt | – | 0,32 |

- Requirement'a bağlı önerilerin rakamları `reports/effort/` ile birebir aynı (ör. G60 koltuk 4,58 %, menzil adımı 48,98 %).
- Referans ve alıntıların hepsi doğrulandı.
- Effort düzeltme turu canlıda tetiklenmedi; sahte provider'lı testle doğrulandı.
- Bu branch'in toplam model harcaması 2,01 USD.

## Dikkat
- **G60 US H1 paketi sınırda:** duyarlılık koşularının % 31'inde major revision'a çıkıyor. Raporda PM için flag olarak duruyor.
- **Analistin kendi profilleri varsayım üstüne varsayım.** KR'de iki yazılım değişikliğinde carryover dedi; katalog terimi eşleşmedikçe bunu kontrol eden bir şey yok.
- Bu profiller sadece analiz dosyasında duruyor; `config/effort/requirements/`'a yazılmıyor.
- Paket horizon'unu aşarsa sadece flag'leniyor; bölmek PM kararı.

Örnekler v3 ile yenilendi: `reports/analysis/G60_US.md`, `F70_GB.md`. Ayrıntı: `reports/step-15-cpm-effort-in-the-analysis.md`.

python3 - <<'EOF'
import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path("tracepoint/agent/analysis.py"); s = p.read_text()
a = s.index('_EFFORT_KEYS = ("effort_pct"'); b = s.index("def run_analysis(")
new = '''_EFFORT_KEYS = ("effort_pct", "p5", "p95", "decision", "decision_stable_pct", "layer", "size")
MAX_CHANGES = 8  # per proposal
MAX_TERMS = 5  # catalogue terms per change


def _flag(level: str, rule: str, text: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    return {"level": level, "rule": rule, "text": text}


def _requirement_in_scope(
    session: Session, requirement_id: str, vehicle: str, market: str
) -> tuple[Requirement | None, str | None]:
    """The requirement a proposal names, or why its profile may not be used. The id comes from
    the model, so it is only accepted for the vehicle and market under analysis."""
    req = session.get(Requirement, requirement_id)
    if req is None or req.status == "withdrawn":
        return None, "which does not exist"
    if (req.vehicle_code, req.market_code) != (vehicle, market):
        return None, f"which belongs to {req.vehicle_code} {req.market_code}, not {vehicle} {market}"
    return req, None


def _analyst_change(c: Change) -> Change:
    """A change written by the model, as the engine may use it: computed as a new development
    (the carryover discount is a claim nobody has checked) and with bounded catalogue terms."""
    terms = [t.strip() for t in c.portfolio_terms if len(t.strip()) >= 4 and not set("%_") & set(t)]
    return c.model_copy(update={"carryover": False, "portfolio_terms": terms[:MAX_TERMS]})


def effort_of_proposals(
    session: Session, vehicle: str, market: str, analysis: SituationAnalysis
) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], list[str]]:
    """Effort of every recommendation and of the H1 and H2 recommendations as packages, computed
    by the CPM engine from the current model. Returns the result and the faults to send back to
    the model.

    Everything the model controls is checked or bounded here, and a proposal that changes the
    vehicle never passes without an estimate silently: it is estimated, or it is a fault and is
    listed as not counted in its package."""
    engine, samples = engine_and_samples(vehicle)
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    faults: list[str] = []
    from_requirements: dict[str, dict[str, list[Change]]] = {"H1": {}, "H2": {}}
    from_analyst: dict[str, list[Change]] = {"H1": [], "H2": []}
    not_counted: dict[str, list[str]] = {"H1": [], "H2": []}
    for rec in analysis.recommendations:
        flags: list[dict[str, str]] = []
        sources: list[str] = []
        req, stored = None, None
        if rec.related_requirement:
            req, problem = _requirement_in_scope(session, rec.related_requirement, vehicle, market)
            if problem:
                text = f"names {rec.related_requirement}, {problem}; its profile is not used"
                flags.append(_flag("conflict", "scope", text))
                faults.append(
                    f'"{rec.title}" {text}. Name a requirement of {vehicle} {market} or set '
                    "related_requirement to null and give effort_changes."
                )
        if req is not None:
            stored = session.get(RequirementEffort, req.id)
            if req.status == "rejected":
                text = f"{req.id} was rejected by the product manager at gate G2"
                flags.append(_flag("conflict", "G2", text))
                faults.append(
                    f'"{rec.title}": {text}. Drop the proposal, or say in the rationale what '
                    "new evidence justifies raising it again."
                )
            elif req.status == "deferred":
                flags.append(_flag("info", "G2", f"{req.id} was deferred by the product manager"))
            if stored is not None and stored.requirement_version != req.version:
                flags.append(
                    _flag(
                        "warning",
                        "63",
                        f"the profile of {req.id} was written for version "
                        f"{stored.requirement_version}; the requirement is at {req.version}",
                    )
                )
        stored_changes = [Change.model_validate(c) for c in stored.changes] if stored else []
        if stored is not None:
            sources.append(f"change profile of {req.id}")
        own = list(rec.effort_changes or [])
        if len(own) > MAX_CHANGES:
            faults.append(
                f'"{rec.title}" lists {len(own)} changes; give at most {MAX_CHANGES}, one per '
                "subsystem where the change starts."
            )
            own = own[:MAX_CHANGES]
        claimed = [c.subsystem for c in own if c.carryover]
        as_written, own = own, [_analyst_change(c) for c in own]
        if own:
            sources.append("analyst's change profile")
        changes = stored_changes + own
        row: dict[str, Any] = {"source": " plus ".join(sources) or None, "flags": flags}
        rows.append(row)
        if not changes:
            # only a declared "nothing changes" passes without an estimate
            if rec.changes_vehicle:
                row["status"] = "missing"
                not_counted[rec.horizon].append(rec.title)
                faults.append(
                    f'"{rec.title}" changes the vehicle but has no change profile'
                    + (f" ({req.id} has none for a vehicle change)" if stored is not None else "")
                    + ". Give effort_changes."
                )
            else:
                row["status"] = "no_vehicle_change"
            continue
        errors = [e for c in changes for e in engine.check_change(c)]
        if errors:
            row.update(status="invalid", error="; ".join(errors))
            not_counted[rec.horizon].append(rec.title)
            faults.append(
                f'The change profile of "{rec.title}" breaks the effort model: '
                f"{row['error']}. Correct effort_changes."
            )
            continue
        res = evaluate_changes(session, engine, samples, vehicle, changes, rec.horizon)
        if claimed:
            with_claim = estimate(engine, stored_changes + as_written).effort
            flags.append(
                _flag(
                    "info",
                    "43",
                    f"carryover claimed by the analyst for {', '.join(claimed)} is not applied: "
                    f"an analyst's profile is computed as a new development (with the claim "
                    f"{with_claim:.2f} %)",
                )
            )
        row.update(
            status="estimated",
            **{k: res[k] for k in _EFFORT_KEYS},
            certification=res["certification_add_on"],
            subsystems=res["subsystems"][:4],
            portfolio=res["portfolio"],
            changes=[c.model_dump() for c in changes],
            flags=flags + res["flags"],
        )
        if stored_changes:
            from_requirements[rec.horizon][req.id] = stored_changes  # named twice: counted once
        from_analyst[rec.horizon] += own
        for flag in res["flags"]:
            if flag["rule"] == "47":
                faults.append(
                    f'"{rec.title}" is {rec.horizon}, but its change profile comes to '
                    f"{row['effort_pct']} % of a new vehicle generation ({row['decision']}): "
                    f"{flag['text']}. Change the horizon, split the proposal, or correct the "
                    "change profile if it overstates the change."
                )
    packages = []
    for horizon in ("H1", "H2"):
        changes = [c for cs in from_requirements[horizon].values() for c in cs]
        changes += from_analyst[horizon]
        in_horizon = [
            r
            for r, rec in zip(rows, analysis.recommendations, strict=True)
            if rec.horizon == horizon and r["status"] == "estimated"
        ]
        if not in_horizon and not not_counted[horizon]:
            continue
        res = evaluate(engine, samples, changes)
        packages.append(
            {
                "horizon": horizon,
                "proposals": len(in_horizon),
                "sum_of_single_pct": round(sum(r["effort_pct"] for r in in_horizon), 2),
                **{k: res[k] for k in _EFFORT_KEYS},
                "certification": res["certification_add_on"],
                "subsystems": res["subsystems"][:6],
                # a package figure that leaves a proposal out says so
                "not_counted": not_counted[horizon],
                # for the product manager to weigh (split the package or accept the class);
                # not sent back to the model, which judges single proposals
                "flags": horizon_flags(
                    horizon, "change", res["decision"], res["decision_stable_pct"]
                )
                if changes
                else [],
            }

def _flag(level: str, rule: str, text: str) -> dict[str, str]:

def _requirement_in_scope(
    session: Session, requirement_id: str, vehicle: str, market: str
) -> tuple[Requirement | None, str | None]:
    """The requirement a proposal names, or why its profile may not be used. The id comes from
    the model, so it is only accepted for the vehicle and market under analysis."""
    req = session.get(Requirement, requirement_id)
    if req is None or req.status == "withdrawn":

    if (req.vehicle_code, req.market_code) != (vehicle, market):
        return None, f"which belongs to {req.vehicle_code} {req.market_code}, not {vehicle} {market}"
    return req, None


def _analyst_change(c: Change) -> Change:
    """A change written by the model, as the engine may use it: computed as a new development
    (the carryover discount is a claim nobody has checked) and with bounded catalogue terms."""
    terms = [t.strip() for t in c.portfolio_terms if len(t.strip()) >= 4 and not set("%_") & set(t)]

content.text:
CPM entegrasyonundaki güvenlik bulgularını kapattım: commit `03659d2` push edildi, PR #15 güncel ve `main` ile çakışmasız. Testler 62 passed, lint temiz, working tree temiz.

İki otomatik inceleme aynı kök sorunu gösterdi: requirement id'si, change profile ve carryover işareti model çıktısı, ve ben bunlara fazla güvenmişim. Bildirimlerde bulguların yalnızca bir kısmının başlığı vardı; görünenleri ve aynı yoldaki benzer açıkları düzelttim.

## Düzeltilenler
- **Kapsam kontrolü:** model hangi requirement id'sini yazarsa onun profili kullanılıyordu; alakasız bir requirement'ın küçük profili ödünç alınabiliyordu. Artık requirement var olmalı, withdrawn olmamalı ve analiz edilen araç + pazara ait olmalı.
- **G2 gate'i:** PM'in reddettiği requirement tekrar önerilirse modele geri gidiyor; deferred olan flag'leniyor.
- **Sessiz atlama yok:** profil verilmeyen öneri "araçta değişiklik yok" diye geçiyor ve horizon kontrolünü atlıyordu. Artık her öneri `changes_vehicle` beyan ediyor; aracı değiştirip kullanılabilir profili olmayan öneri hata sayılıyor ve paketinde "sayılmadı" diye listeleniyor.
- **İkisi de sayılıyor:** öneri hem requirement'a bağlı hem kendi ek değişikliklerini veriyorsa ekler artık atılmıyor.
- **Carryover indirimi uygulanmıyor:** model kendi profilinde carryover diyerek effort'u düşürebiliyordu. Artık iddia raporlanıyor ama hesap yeni geliştirme olarak yapılıyor; iddialı rakam yanında gösteriliyor.
- **Sınırlar:** öneri başına en fazla 8 değişiklik; katalog terimleri en fazla 5, en az 4 karakter, wildcard yok.

## Canlı doğrulama (prompt v4)

| Kapsam | Öneri | Tahmin edilen | Açık hata | H1 paketi | Maliyet (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| G60, pazar US | 8 | 7 | 0 | 13,7 %, adapt (koşuların % 62'sinde) | 0,20 |
| G60, ülke KR | 5 | 4 | 0 | 9,2 %, adapt | 0,13 |
| F70, ülke GB | 7 | 5 | 0 | 8,4 %, adapt | 0,20 |

- KR'de analist üç öneride carryover iddia etti; iddia uygulanmayınca rakamlar 4,4 / 3,4 / 2,4 yerine 4,9 / 4,2 / 2,8 % çıktı.
- Tahmin edilmeyen öneriler açıkça "araçta değişiklik yok" beyanlı (ör. sürüş karakterini koru).
- Branch'in toplam model harcaması 2,54 USD.

## Açık kalan
- Subsystem, own impact ve layer hâlâ modelin yargısı; raporda gerekçesiyle görünüyor ama doğrulanmıyor.
- `changes_vehicle` de modelin beyanı: artık görünür, ama doğrulanmış değil.

Kayıt: `plan/decisions.md` D-072 ve `reports/step-15-cpm-effort-in-the-analysis.md` bölüm 4. Örnekler v4 ile yenilendi.

Bu arada PR #15 merge edilmiş; son güvenlik düzeltmesi merge'den bir commit sonra kaldığı için ayrı bir PR açtım: https://github.com/alpgi1/tracepoint/pull/19

## Durum

- **PR #19 açık, tek düzeltme içeriyor.** Branch `main`'in 2 commit önünde, geride değil; testler 63 passed, lint temiz, working tree temiz.

--- plan 05
# Effort layer, market layer and the domain panel (bridge from Phase 5 to Phase 6)

| Field | Value |

| Version | 0.1 (2026-10-11), proposal for the team, not a decision |
| Audience | Backend (data model, engine, exports), frontend (the screen after the vehicle is chosen), presenters |
| Question answered | After market and vehicle are chosen, the PM must see three things per category: what customers like, what they dislike or miss, and how the market and the competition stand. The team wants to present this "within the CPM engine", and aske
| Inputs | The team's `cpm_engine.py`, the effort metrics pitch, the decision rules v0.2 (rules 1 to 40), the cost rules (rules 41 to 52), `external_sources_v2.json` (54 sources) and `trend_sources.md` (76 sources). None of these files is in the repository yet
| Related | `plan/00-master-plan.md` § 4.2 (layers), § 6 (prioritisation), `plan/06-pm-workspace-ux-spec.md`, `plan/decisions.md` D-012, D-022, D-037, D-060, D-061 |

---

## 0. The answer in one paragraph

Keep the **nine vehicle domains** as the rows of the table on the right. They are already the unit of every
finding, every requirement and every PM decision (D-012, D-022), every level-2 theme maps to exactly one of
them, and they are the grouping BMW's own process slide uses (Exterior, Interior, Powertrain, Driver
assistance). Bring the **twelve CPM subsystems** in as the effort consequence of each candidate change:
which subsystems a change touches, what share of a new vehicle it costs, and whether that is an
adaptation, a major revision or a new generation. Customers speak in domains; effort propagates in
subsystems. Both lenses stay on screen, each where it carries information. The third item the PM needs,
market and competition, is the one layer the repository does not have yet; it is built from the two
source registries as curated, dated evidence, and it feeds the same panel.

---

## 1. Two lenses and the crosswalk between them

### 1.1 Why the nine domains stay the rows

* Every finding (211 for G60 US), every requirement (57 in three scopes) and the baseline reports carry a
  `domain_key`; the taxonomy maps its 225 canonical level-2 themes to one domain each (D-022). A twelve-row table keyed
  by engineering subsystem would need a second mapping of all themes, and the counts would be lopsided:
  customers do not write about the E/E architecture or the body structure; `infotainment_digital` alone
  holds 876 classified rows for G60 US (`reports/baseline/G60_US.json`).
* The brief puts engineering requirements out of scope. A navigation built on engineering subsystems
  signals the wrong lens to the jury; the process slide groups requirements by customer-facing area.
* A change's subsystem footprint is a **set**, computed by the engine (seat ventilation touches Seats,
  Software/HMI, E/E and Thermal), so a single "primary subsystem" row would hide what the engine is for.

### 1.2 Crosswalk (for display and for the change profiles)

| Vehicle domain | CPM subsystems that typically carry its changes |
|---|---|
| Exterior & Design | Exterior design, Paint/color; Body/structure for proportions and wheelbase |
| Interior Comfort & Materials | Seats, Interior/console, Thermal/HVAC; Software/HMI for climate operation |
| Space & Practicality | Body/structure, Interior/console |
| Infotainment & Digital Services | Software/HMI, E/E architecture |
| Driver Assistance & Parking | Software/HMI, E/E architecture (sensors); Chassis for actuators |
| Powertrain, Range & Charging | Powertrain, HV battery, Charging, Thermal/HVAC |
| Driving Experience & Dynamics | Chassis, Powertrain; Software/HMI for drive modes |
| Quality Perception & NVH | Body/structure, Interior/console, Chassis |
| Variant & Package Offering | none: packaging is a K0 configuration change; effort comes from the features it bundles |
| General | none |

Four subsystems (Body/structure, Chassis, E/E architecture, Thermal/HVAC) have no customer domain of their
own; they are reached only through propagation. That is the strongest argument against twelve rows.

### 1.3 If the team still wants twelve rows

lastPrompt: ai flow'una analiz kısmına ve genel pipeline'a entegre ettik mi?

content.text:
Kısmen. AI flow'a ve analize evet; genel pipeline'da üç yerde bağlı, üç yerde değil.

## Bağlı olanlar
- **AI flow (agent loop):** `get_effort` tool'u her agent'a açık. Canlı analizlerde analist onu çağırdı.
- **Analiz:** tam bağlı. Her önerinin effort'unu CPM motoru hesaplıyor, H1/H2 paketleri çıkıyor, horizon'a uymayan öneri düzeltmeye gidiyor.
- **Pipeline, requirement tarafı:** `start.sh` requirement import'tan hemen sonra `effort backtest`, `effort estimate` ve `effort report` çalıştırıyor. 57 requirement'ın effort'u DB'de ve `GET /requirements/{id}` cevabında.

## Bağlı olmayanlar
- **Scoring (Phase 5):** hâlâ yok. `priority_score` boş, yani effort önceliği etkilemiyor. Master plan effort'u skorun negatif faktörü olarak istiyor.
- **Analiz pipeline'ın otomatik adımı değil:** `start.sh` analiz çalıştırmıyor (token harcadığı için). `agent analyze` elle ya da `POST /agent/analyze` ile tetikleniyor.
- **`main`'e yeni gelen CPM dosyaları backend'de kullanılmıyor:** `config/cpm/` altındaki `theme_subsystem_map.yaml` (225 temanın subsystem eşlemesi), `subsystems.yaml` ve `market_context.yaml` PR #17/#18 ile geldi. Şu an sadece frontend okuyor.

## En değerli eksik
Üçüncü madde. Analist şu an kendi önerisinin hangi subsystem'e dokunduğunu kendi yargısıyla yazıyor. `theme_subsystem_map.yaml` bunu veriye bağlayabilir: finding'in teması subsystem'i belirler, model sadece own impact ve layer'ı tahmin eder. Bu, "analist profilleri varsayım üstüne varsayım" sınırını daraltır.

Ayrıca `plan/05-effort-market-layer-and-domain-panel.md` diye bir öneri dokümanı gelmiş (karar değil, ekip önerisi): domain × subsystem crosswalk'u ve henüz olmayan bir market/competition katmanı tarif ediyor. Hiçbiri backend'de uygulanmadı.

Sıradaki adım olarak `theme_subsystem_map`'i analiste bağlamayı öneririm; scoring ayrı ve daha büyük bir iş.

## claude/backend-classification-agent-requirements...origin/claude/backend-classification-agent-requirements
1	0
MERGED
80:| D-073 | 2026-10-11 | The vehicle screen's right column shows the twelve CPM subsystems (body / structure, chassis, powertrain, HV battery, thermal / HVAC, E/E architecture, software / HMI, interior / console, seats, exterior design, paint / colour, charging) instead of the nine-domain complaint list: each row carries the subsystem's weight as a share of a new vehicle's development effort (sum 100, the values of `cost/cpm_engine.py`, marked as assumptions) and the customer rows that fall in it through the theme-to-subsystem mapping; the list is ordered by weight. The domains stay as the label of every theme | Team brief for step 13: the list follows the CPM engine (effort rules 41 to 52); a change is measured by its propagation, not by counting | `config/cpm/subsystems.yaml`, `config/cpm/theme_subsystem_map.yaml`, `frontend/content/cpm.json` built by `frontend/scripts/build-cpm.py`; spec in `plan/07-frontend-plan.md` and `frontend/docs/06-cpm-subsystems.md` |
81:| D-074 | 2026-10-11 | A subsystem row opens a dialog that covers most of the viewport (native `dialog`, `showModal`, no library), with three blocks: what customers like (themes by likes with two Likes verbatims each), what customers criticise (themes by complaints with the defect / difficult to use / wants split and two complaint verbatims each), and the market and competition evidence for the selected market and subsystem (statement, source with date and primary or secondary, evidence level by source count, note, contradiction shown as both sides, basis). Empty layers state that plainly; verbatims are shown as written and the audit's forbidden-text scan skips quoted verbatims | Team brief for step 13; rules 31 to 36 for the evidence rows | `frontend/components/workspace/cpm-dialog.tsx`; the market rows come from `config/cpm/market_context.yaml`, first filled with the four web rows of the rule set v0.2 |
82:| D-075 | 2026-10-11 | The frontend plan v2 (`plan/07-frontend-plan.md`) supersedes `06-pm-workspace-ux-spec.md` for the shell and screens 0 to 2 and fixes the CPM API contract the backend team builds against (`GET /cpm/subsystems`, `GET /cpm/{vehicle}?market=`, later `POST /cpm/effort`); until the endpoints exist the frontend reads `content/cpm.json`, generated from the same `config/cpm/` files the backend engine reads | Team brief: rewrite the frontend plan from the start and code against it; the backend team works in parallel | TypeScript types in `frontend/lib/content/cpm-types.ts` are the contract; the content build and the endpoints must agree on the counting basis (classification rows of the baselines) |

It can be done without breaking the data: give every **feature** (section 2) a primary subsystem and
derive the row counts from features, not from themes. The cost: the long tail of themes that are not in
the feature hub disappears from the likes and dislikes, and the four subsystems above show "engineering
only, no direct customer evidence". The panel content (section 5) is the same in both layouts.

---

## 2. The feature hub: one object that joins the three tabs and the engine

Today the repository has customer themes (level 2), catalogue items (equipment) and requirements, linked
by `config/findings/theme_equipment_map.yaml`. The competitor comparison, the luxury-level rules and the
effort engine all need a **feature** key. Proposal: `config/features/features.yaml`, about twenty entries
to start, each with:

```yaml
features:
  - key: seat_ventilation_front
    name: Front seat ventilation
    domain: interior_comfort
    level2_themes: ["Seating, ventilate / heat"]          # voice of customer
    equipment_terms: [Sitzbelüftung, Komfortsitze]         # BMW catalogue (reuse theme_equipment_map)
    luxury_level: L2            # rules 19 and 20: L1 basic comfort, L2, L3, new (not in any BMW series)
    series_ceiling_ok: [G60, G70]   # F70 ceiling is L1 (rule 20)
    effort:                     # the CPM change profile (section 4)
      source_subsystem: Seats
      own_impact: 0.3
      layer: K2                 # K0 configuration, K1 bolt-on, K2 module, K3 system / platform
      carryover_if: option_exists_on_variant   # rule 43: deterministic portfolio scan
    competitor_feature: seat_ventilation_front # key in the competitor matrix
    trend_topics: [T6]          # cabin comfort family in trend_sources.md
  - key: console_fridge
    name: Centre console fridge
    domain: interior_comfort
    level2_themes: ["Cooling", "Center console, front"]
    equipment_terms: []         # not in any BMW catalogue
    luxury_level: new
    effort: {source_subsystem: Interior/console, own_impact: 0.3, layer: K2, carryover_if: never}
    competitor_feature: console_fridge
    trend_topics: [T6]
    regional_rules: [R7, R8]    # China: higher priority, medium evidence, contradiction shown
  - key: battery_new_generation
    name: New cell and pack generation (real-world range)
    domain: powertrain_range_charging
    level2_themes: ["Electric Range", "High-voltage battery"]
    luxury_level: L1
    effort: {source_subsystem: HV battery, own_impact: 1.0, layer: K3, carryover_if: never}
    competitor_feature: dc_charging_speed
    trend_topics: [T5]
```

Candidates for the first twenty: seat ventilation (front, rear), seat massage, heated steering wheel,
panoramic roof, rear-seat screens, console fridge, head-up display and AR-HUD, physical climate controls,
rotary controller, CarPlay and Android Auto (and CarPlay Ultra), hands-free highway assistant, automatic
parking, NACS port and Supercharger access, DC charging speed, real-world range, zero-gravity seat, ambient
light, digital key, AI assistant, settings that persist over the air, start-stop that stays off. Every
one already appears in the findings or the requirements, so the hub adds no new claims, only joins.

---

## 3. The market and competition layer (the third tab)

### 3.1 Source registries

Convert the two uploaded files into configuration, unchanged in content:

* `config/sources/external_sources.yaml` from `external_sources_v2.json` (54 rows): region, institution,
  category, trust, scope fit, access, URL, status (keep / add / secondary / drop), intended use.
* `config/sources/trend_sources.yaml` from `trend_sources.md` (76 rows): id, family (P, T1 to T8, X),
  regions, publication date, key figure, trust 1 to 4, what it feeds (market momentum, customer pull,
  contradiction input), core or secondary, verification (yes / partly / no).

The registries list sources, not evidence. The next two files hold the evidence.

### 3.2 External evidence items (`config/external/evidence.yaml`)

## 6. After the panel: the decision flow

The three tabs are the situation analysis of the process slide. What follows is its next four stages, and
the repository already has the objects for them.

| Stage on the slide | In the panel | Object |
|---|---|---|
| Structure and context: all potential requirements, implement 0/1 | the candidate list under the tabs, `recommend` true or false with the rationale | `Requirement.recommend` |
| Requirements definition: measurable targets | the criteria table of the candidate (opens inline) | `Requirement.criteria` with `basis` |
| Prioritisation: customer and business | customer impact (rows, severity, study gap), competitive pressure and trend alignment (section 3), effort as the business side (section 4), each a visible component | Phase 5 score components |
| Documentation | the decision sheet and the audit timeline | audit events, D2 export |

**Actions per candidate**: Accept (approve), Reject (reason), Defer to H2 (reason), Comment. Approve,
reject and defer map onto the existing gate G2 endpoint. **Keep** items have Protect (creates a
strength-protection requirement, three already exist) and Carry to another series (rule 17; the
luxury-level check decides whether it is allowed).

**Comment to constraint** (rules 26 to 30): the PM writes free text ("no hybrid", "the fridge has to be
in", "sportier"). The LLM turns it into a typed constraint, `eliminate` / `require` / `prefer` with a
target, and the PM confirms it in one click; when the text is ambiguous the panel asks one short question
(rule 29). The deterministic part then runs: an eliminated powertrain is replaced by the next one in the
region's ranking from `market_context` (rules 11, 27); a required feature enters with its effort and a
warning when it sits above the series ceiling (rules 14 to 20); a preference nudges the weight profile;
dependent requirements are recomputed (a powertrain change toggles the range and charging requirements,
rule 28); the panel shows what changed (rule 30) and every step is an audit event (rule 40). Every
constraint can be withdrawn.

**Proposal tray** (persistent, at the bottom of the workspace): accepted count, combined effort with its

    return yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

"""The twelve CPM subsystems as a view on the evidence (decisions D-073 to D-075).

Customers speak in themes and domains; effort propagates in subsystems. This module joins the two
with the authored mapping ``config/cpm/theme_subsystem_map.yaml``: which classification rows fall
in each subsystem, which themes customers like and criticise there, and what the market and
competitor evidence of ``config/cpm/market_context.yaml`` says about it. The output has the shape
of ``frontend/lib/content/cpm-types.ts``, which is the contract of the ``/cpm`` endpoints, and
feeds the context pack and the tools of the agents.

The mapping, the weights and the links are assumptions, not calibrated (effort rule 50).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections import Counter
from datetime import UTC, date, datetime
from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Literal

import yaml
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from tracepoint.db.models import (
    Finding,
    RequirementFinding,
    TaxonomyLevel2,
    Verbatim,
    VerbatimClassification,
)

Labels = Literal["given", "all"]
COMPLAINT_FIELDS = {"Defect": "defects", "Difficult to Use": "difficultToUse", "Wants": "wants"}
MAX_THEMES = 6
MAX_QUOTES = 2
QUOTE_MIN, QUOTE_MAX, QUOTE_CUT = 40, 240, 300
SURVEY_SOURCE = "Source C"  # survey answers that repeat the question; used when nothing else exists


class _Source(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
    title: str
    url: str
    date: date
    type: Literal["primary", "secondary"]


class MarketRow(BaseModel):
    """One market or competitor statement (rules 31 to 36 of the team's rule set)."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
    market: str
    subsystem: str
    kind: Literal["market", "competitor"]
    statement: str
    source: _Source
    level: Literal["strong", "medium", "weak"]
    basis: Literal["evidence", "assumption"]
    note: str | None = None
    contradiction: dict[Literal["for", "against"], str] | None = None


def cpm_dir() -> Path:
    from tracepoint.core.settings import get_settings

    return get_settings().config_dir / "cpm"


def _read(name: str) -> tuple[Any, float]:
    path = cpm_dir() / name
    return yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")), path.stat().st_mtime


@lru_cache(maxsize=4)
def _catalogue(mtime: float) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return _read("subsystems.yaml")[0]


def load_catalogue() -> dict[str, Any]:
    """``config/cpm/subsystems.yaml``: method, and the subsystems with weight, scope and links."""
    return _catalogue((cpm_dir() / "subsystems.yaml").stat().st_mtime)


def subsystem_names() -> dict[str, str]:
    return {s["key"]: s["name"] for s in load_catalogue()["subsystems"]}


@lru_cache(maxsize=4)
def _theme_map(mtime: float) -> tuple[dict[str, str], tuple[str, ...]]:
    data = _read("theme_subsystem_map.yaml")[0]
    known = set(subsystem_names())
    themes: dict[str, str] = {}
    for key, names in data["map"].items():
        if key not in known:
            raise ValueError(f"theme_subsystem_map.yaml: unknown subsystem {key}")
        for name in names or []:
            if name in themes:
                raise ValueError(f"theme_subsystem_map.yaml: {name!r} is mapped twice")
            themes[name] = key
    unassigned = tuple(data.get("unassigned") or [])
    if set(unassigned) & set(themes):
        raise ValueError("theme_subsystem_map.yaml: a theme is both mapped and unassigned")
    return themes, unassigned


def load_theme_map() -> tuple[dict[str, str], tuple[str, ...]]:
    """(level-2 theme name → subsystem key, themes that belong to no subsystem)."""
    return _theme_map((cpm_dir() / "theme_subsystem_map.yaml").stat().st_mtime)


def theme_subsystem(theme: str | None) -> str | None:
    return load_theme_map()[0].get(theme) if theme else None


def load_market_rows(market: str | None = None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Market and competitor evidence rows, each with a stable id (its position among the rows
    of the same market and subsystem; new rows are appended) and an evidence reference."""
    known = set(subsystem_names())
    seen: Counter = Counter()
    out = []
    for raw in _read("market_context.yaml")[0]["rows"]:
        row = MarketRow.model_validate(raw)
        if row.subsystem not in known:
            raise ValueError(f"market_context.yaml: unknown subsystem {row.subsystem}")
        seen[row.market, row.subsystem] += 1
        rid = f"MKT-{row.market}-{row.subsystem}-{seen[row.market, row.subsystem]}"
        if market and row.market != market:
            continue
        out.append(
            {
                "id": rid,
                "evidence_ref": f"market:{rid}",
                "market": row.market,
                "subsystem": row.subsystem,
                "kind": row.kind,
                "statement": row.statement,
                "source": {**row.source.model_dump(), "date": row.source.date.isoformat()},
                "level": row.level,
                "basis": row.basis,
                "note": row.note,
                "contradiction": row.contradiction,
            }
        )
    return out


def catalogue(session: Session) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The catalogue part of the contract (``CpmCatalogue``): method, subsystems, mapping."""
    data = load_catalogue()
    method = data["method"]
    themes, unassigned = load_theme_map()
    import yaml as _yaml  # domains.yaml is plain configuration

    from tracepoint.core.settings import get_settings

    domains = _yaml.safe_load(
        (get_settings().config_dir / "taxonomy" / "domains.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    )["domains"]
    return {
        "generatedAt": datetime.now(UTC).date().isoformat(),
        "method": {
            "name": method["name"],
            "reference": method["reference"],
            "url": method["url"],
            "engine": "backend/tracepoint/effort/cpm.py",
            "basis": method["basis"],
            "weightSources": method["weight_sources"],
            "thresholds": {
                "adaptBelowPercent": method["thresholds"]["adapt_below_percent"],
                "newGenerationFromPercent": method["thresholds"]["new_generation_from_percent"],
            },
            "certificationAddOnPercent": method["certification_add_on_percent"],
        },
        "subsystems": [
            {
                "key": s["key"],
                "name": s["name"],
                "scope": s["scope"],
                "weight": s["weight"],
                "certificationTrigger": bool(s.get("certification_trigger")),
                "links": s.get("links") or [],
            }
            for s in data["subsystems"]
        ],
        "mapping": {
            "source": "config/cpm/theme_subsystem_map.yaml",
            "themes": len(themes) + len(unassigned),
            "unassigned": sorted(unassigned),
        },
        "marketContextSource": "config/cpm/market_context.yaml",
        "domains": {k: v["name"] for k, v in domains.items()},
    }


def _pick_quotes(cands: list[Verbatim]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Two verbatims per theme and polarity: one per verbatim, sources other than the survey
    first, texts of a readable length, in the order of their ids (as the frontend build does)."""
    unique = list({v.id: v for v in sorted(cands, key=lambda v: v.id)}.values())
    preferred = [
        v for v in unique if v.source_label != SURVEY_SOURCE and QUOTE_MIN <= v.char_len <= QUOTE_MAX
    ]
    return [
        {
            "id": v.id,
            "evidenceRef": f"verbatim:{v.id}",
            "text": v.text if v.char_len <= QUOTE_CUT else v.text[:QUOTE_CUT] + " …",
            "source": v.source_label,
            "powertrain": v.powertrain,
            "country": v.country_code,
        }
        for v in (preferred or [v for v in unique if v.text])[:MAX_QUOTES]
    ]


def subsystem_view(
    session: Session,
    vehicle: str,
    market: str,
    country: str | None = None,
    *,
    labels: Labels = "given",
    subsystem: str | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Per subsystem: classification rows, likes, complaints, the themes customers like and
    criticise with two verbatims each, and the market rows (``CpmView``).

    ``labels`` is the counting basis: ``given`` counts the labels of the workbooks only, as the
    committed baselines and the frontend content do; ``all`` adds the assistant's gap labels
    (D-056), as the baseline builder and the context pack do. ``subsystem`` keeps the totals of
    all twelve and returns the theme detail of that one only."""
    themes, _ = load_theme_map()
    stmt = (
        select(Verbatim, VerbatimClassification.feedback_type, TaxonomyLevel2)
        .join(VerbatimClassification, VerbatimClassification.verbatim_id == Verbatim.id)
        .join(TaxonomyLevel2, TaxonomyLevel2.id == VerbatimClassification.level2_id)
        .where(
            Verbatim.vehicle_code == vehicle,
            Verbatim.market_code == market,
            VerbatimClassification.status == "canonical",
        )
    )
    if country:
        stmt = stmt.where(Verbatim.country_code == country)
    if labels == "given":
        stmt = stmt.where(VerbatimClassification.origin == "given")
    per: dict[str, dict[str, dict[str, Any]]] = {s: {} for s in subsystem_names()}
    rows = unassigned = 0
    verbatim_ids: set[str] = set()
    for v, ftype, theme in session.execute(stmt):
        rows += 1
        verbatim_ids.add(v.id)
        key = themes.get(theme.name)
        if key is None:
            unassigned += 1
            continue
        t = per[key].setdefault(
            theme.name,
            {
                "theme": theme.name,
                "domain": theme.domain_key or "general",
                "rows": 0,
                "likes": 0,
                "complaints": 0,
                "defects": 0,
                "difficultToUse": 0,
                "wants": 0,
                "_liked": [],
                "_criticised": [],
            },
        )
        t["rows"] += 1
        if ftype == "Likes":
            t["likes"] += 1
            t["_liked"].append(v)
        elif ftype in COMPLAINT_FIELDS:
            t["complaints"] += 1
            t[COMPLAINT_FIELDS[ftype]] += 1
            t["_criticised"].append(v)
    market_rows = load_market_rows(market)
    entries = []
    for key, by_theme in per.items():
        detail = subsystem is None or subsystem == key
        liked = sorted(
            (t for t in by_theme.values() if t["likes"]), key=lambda t: (-t["likes"], t["theme"])
        )[:MAX_THEMES]
        criticised = sorted(
            (t for t in by_theme.values() if t["complaints"]),
            key=lambda t: (-t["complaints"], t["theme"]),
        )[:MAX_THEMES]
        entries.append(
            {
                "key": key,
                "rows": sum(t["rows"] for t in by_theme.values()),
                "likes": sum(t["likes"] for t in by_theme.values()),
                "complaints": sum(t["complaints"] for t in by_theme.values()),
                "themes": len(by_theme),
                "liked": [
                    {
                        **{k: t[k] for k in ("theme", "domain", "rows", "likes")},
                        "quotes": _pick_quotes(t["_liked"]) if detail else [],
                    }
                    for t in liked
                ],
                "criticised": [
                    {
                        **{
                            k: t[k]
                            for k in (
                                "theme",
                                "domain",
                                "rows",
                                "complaints",
                                "defects",
                                "difficultToUse",
                                "wants",
                            )
                        },
                        "quotes": _pick_quotes(t["_criticised"]) if detail else [],
                    }
                    for t in criticised
                ],
                "market": [r for r in market_rows if r["subsystem"] == key],
            }
        )
    basis = (
        "labels given in the feedback workbook"
        if labels == "given"
        else "labels given in the workbook plus the assistant's gap labels (D-056)"
    )
    return {
        "vehicle": vehicle,
        "market": market,
        "country": country,
        "verbatims": len(verbatim_ids),
        "rows": rows,
        "unassignedRows": unassigned,
        "rowsSource": f"classification rows with a canonical level-2 theme, {basis}; theme to "
        "subsystem by config/cpm/theme_subsystem_map.yaml (an assumption)"
        if rows
        else "no classified verbatims for this vehicle in this scope",
        "subsystems": entries,
    }


def subsystems_of_refs(session: Session, refs: list[str]) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Subsystems the cited evidence sits in, with the number of references per subsystem:
    verbatims through their labels, findings and requirements through their themes, market rows
    by their own subsystem. Study metrics, catalogue items and sales carry no theme."""
    themes, _ = load_theme_map()
    market = {r["evidence_ref"]: r["subsystem"] for r in load_market_rows()}
    verbatims = [r.split(":", 1)[1] for r in refs if r.startswith("verbatim:")]
    findings = [r for r in refs if r.startswith("FND-")]
    requirements = [r for r in refs if r.startswith("REQ-")]
    hits: Counter = Counter(market[r] for r in refs if r in market)
    if verbatims:
        labelled = session.execute(
            select(VerbatimClassification.verbatim_id, TaxonomyLevel2.name)
            .join(TaxonomyLevel2, TaxonomyLevel2.id == VerbatimClassification.level2_id)
            .where(
                VerbatimClassification.verbatim_id.in_(verbatims),
                VerbatimClassification.status == "canonical",
            )
        ).all()
        hits.update(s for _, s in {(vid, themes.get(name)) for vid, name in labelled} if s)
    by_requirement: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
    if requirements:
        for rid, fid in session.execute(
            select(RequirementFinding.requirement_id, RequirementFinding.finding_id).where(
                RequirementFinding.requirement_id.in_(requirements),
                RequirementFinding.role != "context",
            )
        ):
            by_requirement.setdefault(rid, set()).add(fid)
    wanted = set(findings) | {f for fs in by_requirement.values() for f in fs}
    finding_subsystem: dict[str, str] = {}
    if wanted:
        for fid, name in session.execute(
            select(Finding.id, TaxonomyLevel2.name)
            .join(TaxonomyLevel2, TaxonomyLevel2.id == Finding.theme_level2_id)
            .where(Finding.id.in_(wanted))
        ):
            if name in themes:
                finding_subsystem[fid] = themes[name]
    hits.update(finding_subsystem[f] for f in findings if f in finding_subsystem)
    for fids in by_requirement.values():
        hits.update({finding_subsystem[f] for f in fids if f in finding_subsystem})
    names = subsystem_names()
    return {k: hits[k] for k in names if hits[k]}
