python3 - <<'EOF'
p='tracepoint/ingest/external.py'
s=open(p,encoding='utf-8').read()
a=s.index('def verify_claim(claim: dict[str, Any], pages: list[str] | None) -> dict[str, Any]:')
b=s.index('# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Fetch and verify (network), then load (offline)')
new='''def verify_claim(claim: dict[str, Any], pages: list[str] | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Does the page say what the claim says? A number alone proves little on a page full of
    numbers, so the figures of a claim have to stand together.

    confirmed: every figure stands in one passage, or a reader pinned the claim with a quote
    that is on the page and every figure is there too; on_page: every figure is on the page,
    but in different passages and nobody pinned it; partial: some figures are missing;
    not_found: no figure, or the quote is not on the page; not_checkable: the claim has neither
    figure nor quote; not_fetched: there is no snapshot."""
    if pages is None:
        return {"verification": "not_fetched"}
    text = " ".join("\\n".join(pages).split())
    quote = claim.get("quote")
    if quote:
        needle = _not_alnum.sub(" ", quote.lower()).strip()
        if not needle or needle not in _not_alnum.sub(" ", text.lower()):
            return {"verification": "not_found", "missing": [f"quote: {quote}"]}
    if not claim["figures"]:
        return {"verification": "confirmed", "excerpt": quote} if quote else {
            "verification": "not_checkable"
        }
    hits = {f: [m.start() for m in _figure_pattern(f).finditer(text)] for f in claim["figures"]}
    found = [f for f, at in hits.items() if at]
    if not found:
        return {"verification": "not_found", "missing": claim["figures"]}

    def together(start: int) -> int:
        return sum(any(start <= p < start + EXCERPT_WINDOW for p in at) for at in hits.values())

    best = max(sorted(p for at in hits.values() for p in at), key=together)
    lo = max(0, best - 100)
    if len(found) < len(hits):
        state = "partial"
    elif together(best) == len(hits) or quote:
        state = "confirmed"
    else:
        state = "on_page"
    return {
        "verification": state,
        "found": found,
        "missing": [f for f in hits if f not in found],
        "excerpt": quote or text[lo : best + EXCERPT_WINDOW],
    }


'''
s=s[:a]+new+s[b:]
s=s.replace("EXCERPT_WINDOW = 420\n","EXCERPT_WINDOW = 600  # the figures of a claim stand together within this many characters\n",1)
s=s.replace('''    # confirmed / partial / not_found''','''    # confirmed / on_page / partial / not_found''')
open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s)

p='tracepoint/db/models.py'
s=open(p,encoding='utf-8').read()
old="    # confirmed / partial / not_found / not_checkable / not_fetched / computed (from an API)"
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,"    # confirmed / on_page / partial / not_found / not_checkable / not_fetched / computed (API)",1)
open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s)

p='tests/test_external.py'
s=open(p,encoding='utf-8').read()
a=s.index('def test_claim_check_against_a_page():')
b=s.index('def test_page_text_keeps_the_article_and_drops_the_chrome():')
new='''def test_claim_check_against_a_page():
    claim = {"figures": ["17.4", "216000", "28"], "quote": None}
    page = "Battery-electric cars took 17,4% of the market. Hybrids sold 216,000 units; 128 new."
    got = verify_claim(claim, [page])
    assert got["verification"] == "partial"
    assert (got["found"], got["missing"]) == (["17.4", "216000"], ["28"])  # 128 is not 28
    assert "17,4%" in got["excerpt"]
    assert verify_claim(claim, [page + " A share of 28 %."])["verification"] == "confirmed"
    # the same figures far apart prove little on a page of numbers, unless a reader pinned it
    apart = [page + " filler" * 200 + " A share of 28 %."]
    assert verify_claim(claim, apart)["verification"] == "on_page"
    pinned = {**claim, "quote": "Hybrids sold 216,000 units"}
    assert verify_claim(pinned, apart)["verification"] == "confirmed"
    assert verify_claim({**claim, "quote": "not there"}, apart)["verification"] == "not_found"
    assert verify_claim(claim, ["nothing here"])["verification"] == "not_found"
    assert verify_claim(claim, None)["verification"] == "not_fetched"
    worded = {"figures": [], "quote": "Nobody asked for the knob"}
    assert verify_claim(worded, ["BMW says: nobody asked for the knob."])["verification"] == (
        "confirmed"
    )
    assert verify_claim({"figures": [], "quote": None}, ["x"])["verification"] == "not_checkable"


'''
s=s[:a]+new+s[b:]
s=s.replace('''    states = {"confirmed", "partial", "not_found", "not_checkable", "not_fetched"}''','''    states = {"confirmed", "on_page", "partial", "not_found", "not_checkable", "not_fetched"}''',1)
open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s)
EOF

from tracepoint.agent.context_pack import build_context_pack, render_markdown

Settings are read from environment variables with the `TRACEPOINT_` prefix or a `.env` file at the
repository root (see `.env.example`).

## Commands

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `tracepoint db init` / `db reset --yes` | create / recreate the schema |
| `tracepoint taxonomy extract` | extract the canonical VFC lists and apply the authored domain map and polarity rules |
| `tracepoint ingest reference` | load vehicles, markets, countries and the taxonomy from `config/` |
| `tracepoint ingest verbatims` / `studies` / `sales` / `optionlists` / `documents` / `all` | ingest the input files (idempotent per vehicle); `documents` reads the BMW Group Report page by page and is skipped while the file is unchanged |
| `tracepoint report baseline --vehicle G60 --market US --out-dir ../reports/baseline` | baseline situation-analysis report (Markdown + JSON) |
| `tracepoint audit export --format json\|csv [--out file]` | export the audit event log |
| `tracepoint classify import [--vehicle G60]` | apply the committed gap labels in `config/classifications/<vehicle>_gaps.jsonl` (no API call; also run by `ingest all`) |
| `tracepoint classify gaps --vehicle G60 [--limit N] [--dry-run]` | LLM gap classification of unclassified rows (dry run: prompts and token estimate only) |
| `tracepoint classify segments --vehicle G60 [--dry-run]` | LLM segmentation of Source B notes into product / process statements |
| `tracepoint classify prepare-sample --vehicle G60` | write the blind-validation sample to `config/validation/` |
| `tracepoint classify validate --vehicle G60` | blind re-classification of the sample; writes `reports/validation/` |
| `tracepoint findings extract --vehicle G60 --market US` | deterministic finding extraction (voice of customer, study metrics, equipment gaps, links) |
| `tracepoint findings report --vehicle G60 --market US --out-dir ../reports/findings` | Markdown finding list |
| `tracepoint requirements import` | load `config/requirements/*.yaml` (validated against the findings, versioned, audited) and replay the G2 decisions in `config/decisions/requirements.jsonl` |
| `tracepoint requirements decide REQ-G60-US-IC-01 approve --note "…"` | gate G2 (approve / reject / defer) on the current version; logged and appended to the decisions file. Also `POST /requirements/{id}/decision` |
| `tracepoint requirements export [--vehicle G60 --market US]` | requirement list (deliverable D2) as Markdown and CSV in `data/requirements/`; API `GET /requirements`, `GET /requirements/{id}` (traceability to findings and evidence, event history) |
| `tracepoint effort backtest [--scope all\|matrix]` | CPM effort engine back-test against the documented BMW decisions in `config/effort/anchors.yaml` (no database; exit code 1 if an anchor fails) |
| `tracepoint effort estimate` | effort of every requirement from `config/effort/requirements/*.yaml` and the model `config/effort/model.yaml`: % of a new vehicle, P5–P95, layer K0–K3, decision, affected subsystems, portfolio scan of the catalogues, horizon ch
| `tracepoint effort report [--vehicle G60 --market US]` | Markdown per vehicle × market (variations H1 / H2 / all, requirements, PM flags, subsystems) in `data/effort/` |
| `tracepoint agent packs [--vehicle G60]` | context pack (JSON + Markdown) per vehicle × market with evidence, written to `data/context_packs/` |
| `tracepoint agent tools` | tool definitions for an LLM agent (name, description, JSON input schema) |
| `tracepoint agent call search_evidence '{"query": "charging flap", "vehicle": "G60"}'` | run one agent tool; every call is an audit event (`tool.called`). Also over HTTP: `GET /agent/tools`, `POST /agent/tools/{name}` |
| `tracepoint agent analyze --vehicle G60 --market US` / `--vehicle F70 --country GB` | situation analysis by the analyst agent (LLM with tool calls, needs the OpenAI key): Markdown and JSON in `data/analyses/`, every insight with its evidence references, ever
| `GET /cpm/{vehicle}?market=US`, `GET /effort/model`, `POST /effort/estimate`, `GET /requirements/{id}/effort` | the CPM contract of `plan/07-frontend-plan.md`: per subsystem the customer rows, liked and criticised blocks with narration, and market evidence (
| `tracepoint settings` | print the effective settings |

"| D-080 | 2026-10-11 | External evidence (Phase 2) starts from the team's two lists, kept in `docs/` as written (Turkish): `trend_sources.md` (76 sources, ids P-01 to X-09) and `external_sources_v2.json` (55 sources, ids E-01 to E-55 by position). `config/external/evidence.yaml` is the authored reading: every entry is either in scope or excluded with a reason, and `tracepoint ingest external` refuses to run while an entry is undecided. In scope is what customers require of the product in EU, US and CN for F70, G60, G68 and G70, and the market and competition around it; out are regulation as a requirement, engineering and defect statistics, pricing, financing and business case, and entries without a customer, market or product statement. 7 entries are excluded (the three the list itself drops, leasing attitudes, an executive survey, patent statistics, a lamp regulation). A source carries an English title, the institution the data comes from and one claim per statement with regions, CPM subsystems, vehicles, kind, topic and basis; tables `external_source` and `external_evidence`, a `source` row per source | Team request: read the two files, store what is useful for the programme in the database in a usable form, and nothing outside the scope of the vehicles and the programme. `plan/05` proposed two registry files and one evidence file; the lists are parseable as they are, so they are not copied into `config/` | The four rows of `config/cpm/market_context.yaml` stay as they are (the frontend content is built from them, D-078); they overlap with P-01, P-03 and T6-07, which now exist from the primary source. Region is kept as the list gives it; a row about a vehicle shows only in its own market |",
"| D-081 | 2026-10-11 | Snapshots (refines D-007 under D-057): a page is fetched once by an identified client (`TracepointResearch`, repository URL in the user agent), which obeys robots.txt, waits between two requests to a host and never retries or works around a refusal. Sources behind a paywall or whose terms forbid automated collection are not fetched (`fetch: manual`); a home page without addressed content is not fetched either. The raw page stays in `data/external/<id>/` and is not committed (third-party text). What each URL returned (status, checksum, time) and the result of every claim check are committed as `config/external/fetched.json`, so a rebuild without the cache gives the same sources and claims. Page text enters the database only for sources about one of our four vehicles (expert reviews, specification pages, NHTSA complaints), as `document_page` rows found by `search_documents`. Two public APIs are read for our vehicles only: NHTSA owner complaints and EPA range and consumption | D-007 asked for snapshots in the database; D-057 made the database a derived artefact, so the committed part has to be files. Industry-wide pages hold much that is outside the scope (trucks, other industries), so only their claims are stored, each with the passage it stands in | `ingest all` and `start.sh` never touch the network; `ingest external --fetch` does. Without the cache the searchable page text is missing until `--fetch` ran once |",
"| D-082 | 2026-10-11 | A claim is checked against its page, and the list's own columns (trust 1 to 4, verified yes / partly / no) are kept beside the result. `confirmed`: every figure of the claim stands in one passage of 600 characters, or a reader pinned the claim with a quote that is on the page and every figure is there too; `on_page`: every figure is there, but apart and unpinned; `partial`, `not_found`, `not_checkable` (no figure, no quote), `not_fetched`; `computed` for claims built from an API. Where the page says something else than the list, the statement follows the page and the difference is a comment in the file. The evidence level follows rule 34 on topics: the number of independent institutions that state the same thing for a shared region (one weak, two medium, three or more strong), where another institution counts only if its statement was confirmed, and two outlets reporting one study are one institution. Forecasts carry `basis: assumption` (rule 36); the nine contradictions of the trend list and one between the testers of the G60 are stored with both sides (rule 35) | A number alone proves little on a page full of numbers (the Deloitte study matches any two-digit figure); the first check counted figures anywhere on the page and confirmed claims the page did not make | First run: 118 authored claims, 81 confirmed, 30 not fetched, 4 not checkable, 3 not found, plus 25 computed; six figures of the lists were corrected or dropped against their pages (`reports/step-17`) |",
"| D-083 | 2026-10-11 | The analyst reads external evidence through one tool and the same rules as market rows: `get_external_evidence` (market, vehicle, subsystem, topic, kind) returns the rows of the market and the worldwide ones, without rows about another vehicle or about subsystems the vehicle does not have; references are `external:EXT-<source>-<n>`; `search_documents` also searches the stored pages and takes a vehicle; the context pack (`context-pack-v4`) says how many rows a scope has, per subsystem and topic; prompt `situation-analysis-v7` adds: an unverified row never carries a recommendation alone, a worldwide row describes no single market, third-party rows about the vehicle are not BMW customer feedback and change no complaint count. In the check of where a change starts (D-079) an external row counts like a verbatim, because it can bear on several subsystems | Stored evidence the analyst cannot reach is not usable; the market layer had four rows | The scoring factors of the trend list (market momentum, customer pull, evidence quality, recency, contradiction penalty) are stored per source (`feeds`, trust, date) and not computed: scoring is Phase 5 |",
]
open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s+'\n'+'\n'.join(rows)+'\n')
EOF

import json
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from tracepoint.ingest.external import load_registry, load_fetched
r=load_registry(); f=load_fetched()
ex=r['excluded']; srcs={s['ref']:s for s in r['sources']}
fam=defaultdict(Counter)
names={'P':'Powertrain share','T5':'Electrification experience','T8':'Ownership model and offer','T1':'Cockpit and HMI','T2':'In-car AI and digital services','T3':'Phone and ecosystem integration','T4':'Driver assistance experience','T6':'Cabin comfort and well-being','T7':'Materials, design, sustainability','X':'Cross-cutting'}
for e in r['listed']:
    k=e['family'] if e['list'].startswith('trend') else 'list: '+e['family']
    fam[k]['listed']+=1
    if e['ref'] in ex: fam[k]['excluded']+=1; continue
    s=srcs[e['ref']]; fam[k]['in_scope']+=1
    st=f['sources'].get(e['ref'],{}).get('status')
    if s['fetch'] in ('auto','api'): fam[k]['attempted']+=1
    if st=='fetched': fam[k]['fetched']+=1
for c in r['claims']:
    e=srcs[c['ref']]; k=e['family'] if e['list'].startswith('trend') else 'list: '+e['family']
    fam[k]['claims']+=1
    v=f['claims'].get(c['id'],{}).get('verification','not_fetched'); fam[k][v]+=1
tot=Counter()
for k,v in fam.items():
    print(f"| {names.get(k,k)} | {v['listed']} | {v['excluded']} | {v['in_scope']} | {v['attempted']} | {v['fetched']} | {v['claims']} | {v['confirmed']} | {v['not_fetched']} | {v['not_found']+v['not_checkable']} |"); tot.update(v)
print(dict(tot))
print("not attempted:", [(s['ref'], s['fetch']) for s in r['sources'] if s['fetch'] in ('manual','none')])
print("failed:", sorted((v['status'], k) for k,v in f['sources'].items() if v['status']!='fetched'))
print("claims per region:", Counter(x for c in r['claims'] for x in c['regions']))
EOF

# Step 17 – External evidence from the team's two source lists

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Date | 2026-10-11 |
| Author | Claude (AI assistant), on request of the team |
| Status | Done – 124 sources and 143 claims in the database, 72 of 100 pages fetched, 81 tests passed, one live analysis |
| Why | The team added `docs/trend_sources.md` and `docs/external_sources_v2.json` and asked to read them, to store what is useful for the programme in the database in a usable form, to fetch the content behind the links, and to add nothing outside the scope of the vehicles and the programme. Until now the market layer was four rows in `config/cpm/market_context.yaml` |

## 1. Delivered

Decisions D-080 to D-083. This is the first part of Phase 2 of the master plan (external evidence
ingestion, D-007).

### 1.1 What the two files are

* `docs/trend_sources.md`: 76 trend sources in ten families (powertrain share, electrification,
  ownership, cockpit, in-car AI, phone integration, driver assistance, cabin comfort, materials,
  cross-cutting), each with region, date, one cell of key figures, a trust grade 1 to 4, what it
  feeds (market momentum, customer pull, contradiction input), core or secondary, and whether
  the list's author verified it. It ends with nine contradictions to keep.
* `docs/external_sources_v2.json`: 55 sources (expert tests, owner voice, quality indices,
  competitor specification, trend) with trust, scope fit, access terms, a status (keep, add,
  secondary, replace, drop) and the intended use. Most entries point to a source, a few carry a
  figure in their description.

Both are in Turkish and stay in `docs/` as written. They are parsed directly; the second list has
no ids, so an entry is `E-<position>`.

### 1.2 The scope decision (`config/external/evidence.yaml`)

Every one of the 131 entries is decided in one authored file: in scope, or excluded with the
reason. `tracepoint ingest external` refuses to run while an entry is undecided, so a row added
to a list cannot reach the database unread.

In scope (step 01, section 1.1): what customers require of the product in the markets we hold
data for, for F70, G60, G68 and G70, and the market and competition around it.

| Excluded | Reason |
|---|---|
| E-07 DEKRA, E-08 TÜV, E-23 C-IASI | dropped by the list itself: defect statistics, crash safety and repair cost |
| T8-02 Ayvens leasing attitudes | a financing channel, not a requirement on the product |
| X-04 KPMG executive survey | executives about their own plans; no customer, market or product statement |
| X-05 WIPO patent statistics | technology activity, not customer or market evidence |
| T7-06 ban on blue driver-assistance lamps in China | regulation of a lamp none of our vehicles carries |

Scope is also applied inside a source:

* the blue-lamp figure of T7-05 is left out with T7-06;
* the Driver Power survey ranks a "1 Series Mk3", the generation before the F70, so only the
  5 Series row is taken;
* page text is stored only for sources about one of our four vehicles. An industry report holds
  trucks, buses and other industries; from those only the claims are stored, each with the
  passage it stands in;
* a row about a vehicle shows only for that vehicle, and a row that bears only on the battery or
  on charging does not show for the F70, which has neither (`config/effort/model.yaml`).

### 1.3 What is stored

| Table | Rows | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `source` (kind `web_page` / `web_api`) | 124 | title, URL, layer, checksum and time of the snapshot, trust and primary / secondary, access terms |
| `external_source` | 124 | id in the list, family, institution the data comes from, regions, vehicles, trust, status, publication date, what the fetch returned, the list's own columns |
| `external_evidence` | 143 | one statement each: kind, regions, CPM subsystems, vehicles, topic, basis, evidence level, verification, the passage on the page, the contradiction it belongs to, URL and checksum |
| `document_page` | 182 | searchable text of the sources about our vehicles: 107 NHTSA complaints and 75 parts of eight pages |

Claims by kind: consumer survey 41, market share 24, official specification 23, competitor move
20, BMW's own offer 8, quality index 8, expert test 7, owner voice 5, infrastructure 3, market
context 2, regulation as context 2. By region: US 76, CN 56, EU 44, worldwide 38 (a claim can
hold for several). By subsystem: software / HMI 64, powertrain 34, interior / console 22, HV
battery 21, charging 15, seats 9, the rest below 7. 42 claims name one of our vehicles (G60 23,
G70 19, G68 4, F70 1); 100 describe a market.

### 1.4 Fetching (D-081)

One client that says who it is, obeys robots.txt, waits a second between two requests to a host,
fetches a page once and never retries or works around a refusal.

| Result | Sources |
|---|---|
| fetched and read | 72 (70 pages and PDFs, 2 APIs) |
| refused with HTTP 403 | 10: Edmunds (E-09, E-13, E-38, E-46), J.D. Power APEAL and valuation (E-10, T8-01), Argonne (P-07), WardsAuto (T4-03), Tech Brew (T4-07), GM Authority (T8-05) |
| no answer within 40 s | 10: Business Wire (T8-03, T1-05, T1-06, T3-05, T6-01, T7-05), McKinsey (T2-02, T2-03, T7-02, E-34) |
| HTTP 468 | 4: Gasgoo (T5-10, T2-05, T4-05, T6-02) |
| page built by script, no text | 2: Shell (T5-05), Autohome equipment matrix (E-51) |
| HTTP 404 | 1: AutoPacific (T4-02) |
| disallowed by robots.txt | 1: EY full report (X-02) |
| not attempted, home page only | 20 |
| not attempted, paywall or collection forbidden | 4: Consumer Reports (E-15, E-39), EV Database (E-28), Bimmerpost (E-47) |

The raw pages are in `data/external/` (58 MB, not committed). `config/external/fetched.json`
(committed) holds what each URL returned and the result of every claim check, so a rebuild on
another machine gives the same sources and claims without the network.

Two public APIs are read for our vehicles only:

* **NHTSA owner complaints**: 107 complaints, 49 for the G60 (i5, 530i, 540i, 550e; model years
  2024 to 2026) and 58 for the G70 (7 Series, i7; 2023 to 2026). The component named most often
  is the service brakes (25 and 31), then stability control and the electrical system. They are
  defect and safety reports, not a satisfaction measure, and are stored as such.
* **EPA range and consumption**: 98 US variants, model years 2023 to 2027, one claim per vehicle,
  model year and kind of drive. Example: the i5 eDrive40 on 19-inch wheels is rated 295 miles
  for 2024 and 2025, 310 for 2026 and 328 for 2027; on 21-inch wheels 270 to 280.

### 1.5 The check of a claim against its page (D-082)

| Result | Claims | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| confirmed | 81 | every figure stands in one passage, or the claim is pinned with a quote from the page and every figure is there |
| computed | 25 | built from an API answer |
| not fetched | 30 | the page could not be read; the list's figure stands unverified |
| not checkable | 4 | kept apart as "by the list, not on the fetched page" |
| not found | 3 | the page does not hold the figures (E-04, T7-04, X-03) |

The first version of the check counted a figure anywhere on the page. The Deloitte study showed
why that is worthless: a PDF of percentage tables matches any two-digit number. Figures now have
to stand together, and where they stand in different paragraphs the claim is pinned by a quote
that was read on the page.

Reading the pages changed the lists in eight places:

| Entry | The list says | The page says |
|---|---|---|
| T5-04 | Europe about 15 electric cars per public charging point | EU 11; 15 is the worldwide ratio expected for 2035 |
| P-03 | China 2025: new energy share 53.9 % | only monthly shares (December 59.1 %); the 53.9 % on the page is August 2024 |
| T5-03 | first 1,000 V models on sale | not on the page |
| T5-09 | about half of China's public network is fast charging | not on the page; it counts 1.1 million new public points in 2025 against the IEA's 1.8 million |
| T3-06 | Huawei HMS for Car in more than 70 models | not on the page |
| T6-03 | zero-gravity seats and switchable glass at Auto China 2026 | not in the slides |
| E-01 | BMW 1 Series in 6th place | "1 Series Mk3", the previous generation, not the F70 |
| E-18 | 7 Series rating 4.36 | another page; this one is the 5 Series |

Four more statements are kept apart with the wording "by the list, not on the fetched page"
(Mercedes-Benz and Chinese makers returning to buttons, the compilation of AI assistants, falling
interest in BMW, Mercedes-Benz and Audi in China, 12 % failed DC charging sessions).

**Evidence level** (rule 34): the number of independent institutions that state the same thing
for a shared region, counted on 33 topics. Another institution counts only if its statement was
confirmed, and two outlets reporting one study are one institution. Result: weak 87, medium 13,
strong 43. Strong topics: powertrain mix, EV outlook, physical controls, hands-free driving,
phone mirroring, AI assistant, driver assistance in China. Seven forecasts carry
`basis: assumption` (rule 36).

**Contradictions** (rule 35): the nine of the trend list, with both sides and the claims they
rest on, and one that the pages added: What Car? calls the infotainment of the 5 Series
class-leading, Autocar calls it convoluted.

### 1.6 What it says about our vehicles

Read on the pages, each a row with its passage:

* **G60, UK owners** (Driver Power 2026): 17th of 50. Second-best car in the survey for
  front-seat comfort, eighth for driving pleasure, top 10 for navigation and connectivity;
  handling 35th, running costs 49th, value 48th, reliability "poor". Front-seat comfort is the
  largest interior complaint of the US verbatims; the two markets disagree.
* **G60, testers**: Autocar finds the climate controls "almost entirely digital" and reports that
  all testers had to look away from the road; Auto Express dislikes setting the air-flow
  direction in a menu; ADAC grades the i5 eDrive40 1.6 overall and names weak points in
  operation and only average charging power. The same theme as the largest US complaint group.
* **G60 and G70, US sales of the electric variants** (Cox Automotive): i5 964 in the second
  quarter of 2026 (down 32.8 %), i7 510 (down 37.8 %). The sales workbook has no powertrain
  split; this is the first one.
* **G60 and G70, US charging**: Tesla Superchargers since 10 December 2025, about 180,000 public
  points in North America.
* **G70**: the next generation of driver assistance brings the hands-free Highway Assistant from
  one European country to more than 20, the 7 Series among the models; BMWBLOG expects the
  facelift to bring a passenger display.
* **G68, China**: Autohome owner rating 4.46 of 5, behind the Audi A6L and the Volvo S90 at 4.50;
  owners praise steering, acceleration and rear room and criticise the centre tunnel in the
  rear, low-speed smoothness and tyre noise. The first owner voice for China in the database.

### 1.7 In the analysis flow (D-083)

* Tool `get_external_evidence` (market, vehicle, subsystem, topic, kind): the rows of the market
  and the worldwide ones, rows about the vehicle first, the EPA tables last. Reachable over HTTP
  as `POST /agent/tools/get_external_evidence`.
* `search_documents` also searches the stored pages and takes a vehicle.
* Context pack `context-pack-v4`: how many rows the scope has, per subsystem and topic.
* Prompt `situation-analysis-v7`: the rules for market rows hold; a row that is not confirmed
  never carries a recommendation alone; a worldwide row describes no single market; rows about
  the vehicle are third-party statements and change no complaint count.
* References `external:EXT-<source>-<n>`; in the check of where a change starts (D-079) an
  external row counts like a verbatim.

## 2. Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `uv run pytest -q` | 81 passed (72 before, 9 new in `tests/test_external.py`) |
| `uv run ruff check`, `ruff format --check` | clean |
| every entry of the two lists decided | 131 = 124 in scope + 7 excluded; the test fails on an undecided entry |
| excluded entries absent from the database | tested for all seven |
| page text only for sources about our vehicles | tested |
| reload | idempotent; a second run gives the same counts |
| live analysis G60 / US | section 3 |

Rows per scope (market rows plus worldwide rows, after the vehicle filter):

| Scope | Rows | About the vehicle | Not confirmed |
|---|---|---|---|
| G60 US | 79 | 17 | 19 |
| G60 EU | 63 | 6 | 17 |
| G70 US | 79 | 17 | 18 |
| G70 EU | 60 | 3 | 17 |
| G70 CN | 74 | 1 | 22 |
| G68 CN | 77 | 4 | 23 |
| F70 EU | 51 | 1 | 15 |

## 3. Live analysis with the external evidence

ANALYSIS_SECTION

## 4. Known limitations

* 28 of 100 pages could not be read, among them every Edmunds page (expert and long-term test of
  the i5) and six Business Wire releases. Their claims stand as "not fetched" with the list's
  figure. Reading them is manual work; a browser session is not built.
* The check proves that the figures stand together on the page, not that the sentence means what
  the claim says. Every confirmed claim was read once by the assistant, not by a second reader.
* The topics behind the evidence level are authored and coarse: "hands-free driving" joins
  demand surveys and competitor fleets. A strong level says that several institutions point the
  same way, not that they measured the same thing.
* A row about a vehicle shows only in its own market. The British tests of the G60 do not appear
  in a US analysis although the cockpit is the same.
* Chinese pages are stored as they are; the full-text search is English, so their text is found
  only through the claims.
* The Sohu review page pools every model year since 2001, and the Autohome page gave the rating
  and the review tags but not the single reviews. China still has no verbatims.
* The competitor matrix of `plan/05` (feature by rival) is not built: the price lists are home
  pages in the list, and unknown cells stay unknown.
* The four rows of `config/cpm/market_context.yaml` are untouched because the frontend content is
  built from them; three of them repeat P-01, P-03 and T6-07 from a secondary outlet.
* The trend score of the list (momentum 35, customer pull 35, evidence quality 20, recency 10,
  contradiction penalty) is not computed; its inputs are stored.
* The first probe of four URLs in this session carried the committer's e-mail address in the
  user agent. The client in the repository does not.

## 5. Next step

* Read the ten refused and ten timed-out pages by hand and pin or correct their claims.
* Decide with the frontend whether the subsystem dialog shows external rows, and replace the
  three secondary market rows with their primary sources.
* Phase 5: trend alignment and competitive pressure as score components, from `feeds`, trust,
  date and the contradictions stored here.

  only, that many rows are weak single-source items, some worldwide rather than US, and that no
  unverified row carried a recommendation alone.'''

content.text:
İki dosya okundu, kapsam içindeki her şey veritabanına yüklendi ve agent artık bu veriye ulaşabiliyor. PR #27 açık: https://github.com/alpgi1/tracepoint/pull/27 (81 test geçiyor).

## Veritabanında ne var

| Tablo | Satır | İçerik |
|---|---|---|
| `external_source` (+ `source`) | 124 | Kaynak kaydı: kurum, bölge, araç, güven 1–4, erişim şartı, fetch sonucu |
| `external_evidence` | 143 | Tek tek iddialar: bölge, CPM alt sistemi, araç, konu, kanıt seviyesi, doğrulama durumu, sayfadaki pasaj |
| `document_page` | 182 | Aranabilir metin: 107 NHTSA şikâyeti ve araçlarımızı anlatan 8 sayfanın 75 parçası |

131 girişten 7'si kapsam dışı bırakıldı:
- DEKRA, TÜV ve C-IASI: liste zaten "çıkar" diyor.
- Ayvens leasing anketi: finansman, ürün gereksinimi değil.
- KPMG yönetici anketi: müşteri ya da pazar verisi yok.
- WIPO patent sayıları: teknoloji faaliyeti, müşteri kanıtı değil.
- Çin'in mavi ADAS lambası yasağı: araçlarımızda olmayan bir lamba.

Sayfa metni yalnızca dört aracımızdan birini anlatan kaynaklar için saklandı. Sektör raporlarından sadece iddia ve dayandığı pasaj alındı.

## Fetch sonucu

100 denemeden 72'si indi; 28'i inmedi:
- **403 ile reddeden (10):** Edmunds'un dört sayfası, J.D. Power'ın iki sayfası, Argonne, WardsAuto, Tech Brew, GM Authority.
- **40 saniyede cevap vermeyen (10):** Business Wire (6) ve McKinsey (4).
- **Diğer (8):** Gasgoo HTTP 468 (4), JS ile yüklenen sayfa (2), 404 (1), robots.txt yasağı (1).

Ayrıca 24 kaynak hiç denenmedi: 20'sinde liste yalnızca ana sayfa veriyor, 4'ü paywall ya da "otomatik toplama yasak" (Consumer Reports, EV Database, Bimmerpost). Reddeden siteleri aşmaya çalışmadım.

## Doğrulama

Her iddia kendi sayfasıyla karşılaştırıldı; rakamların aynı pasajda durması gerekiyor.

- 118 elle yazılmış iddia: 81 teyitli, 30 indirilemedi, 4 "listede var, sayfada yok", 3 bulunamadı.
- 25 iddia API'den hesaplandı (NHTSA, EPA).

Sayfaları okuyunca listede 8 yer yanlış ya da desteksiz çıktı:

| Giriş | Liste | Sayfa |
|---|---|---|
| T5-04 | Avrupa'da şarj noktası başına ≈15 EV | AB 11 (15, 2035 dünya tahmini) |
| P-03 | Çin 2025 NEV payı %53,9 | Sayfada yıllık pay yok; %53,9 Ağustos 2024'ün aylık değeri |
| E-01 | 1 Serisi 6. sırada | Sıralanan araç önceki nesil ("Mk3"), F70 değil |
| T5-03 | İlk 1.000 V modeller | Sayfada yok |
| T5-09 | Çin kamu ağının ≈%50'si hızlı | Sayfada yok |
| T3-06 | Huawei HMS 70+ modelde | Sayfada yok |
| T6-03 | Sıfır yerçekimi koltuk, değişken cam | Sunumda yok |
| E-18 | 7 Serisi puanı 4,36 | Başka sayfada |

## Araçlarımız hakkında çıkanlar

- **G60, İngiltere sahipleri (Driver Power 2026):** 50 araç içinde 17. Ön koltuk konforunda 2., sürüş keyfinde 8.; yol tutuş 35., işletme maliyeti 49., güvenilirlik "zayıf". ABD verisinde koltuk en büyük iç mekân şikâyetiydi; iki pazar çelişiyor.
- **G60, uzman testleri:** Autocar'a göre klima kontrolleri "neredeyse tamamen dijital" ve tüm test sürücüleri yoldan gözünü ayırmak zorunda kaldı. ADAC i5'e 1,6 verdi, zayıf yön olarak kullanım ve şarj gücünü yazdı. What Car? ise infotainment'ı "sınıfının en iyisi" buluyor; bu çelişki olarak kaydedildi.
- **ABD BEV satışları (Cox):** i5 2026'nın ikinci çeyreğinde 964 adet (−%32,8), i7 510 adet (−%37,8). Satış dosyasında powertrain ayrımı yoktu; ilk kez var.
- **EPA menzili:** i5 eDrive40, 19 inç jantla 295 mil (2024–25), 310 (2026), 328 (2027).
- **NHTSA:** G60 için 49, G70 için 58 şikâyet; en çok adı geçen parça servis frenleri.
- **G68, Çin (Autohome):** sahip puanı 4,46; Audi A6L ve Volvo S90 4,50. Çin için veritabanındaki ilk sahip sesi.

## Agent tarafı

Yeni tool `get_external_evidence`; `search_documents` artık bu sayfaları da arıyor. Teyitsiz bir satır tek başına öneri taşıyamıyor.

G60/US canlı analizinde 55 referansın 10'u dış kanıttı, bilinmeyen referans yok, maliyet 0,35 USD. Şarj şikâyetlerini "kısmen pazar sorunu" diye okudu: ABD'de şarj noktası başına 33 EV, AB'de 11. Bir uyarı açık kaldı: bir önerinin değişikliği yazılımda başlıyor ama kanıtı şarj alt sisteminde.

## Eksikler

- İnmeyen 28 sayfanın iddiaları listedeki rakamla, "indirilemedi" olarak duruyor; elle okunmaları gerekiyor.
- Teyitli iddiaları sayfada bir kez ben okudum; ikinci bir göz bakmadı.
- Araç-özel satırlar sadece kendi pazarında görünüyor: İngiliz G60 testleri ABD analizine girmiyor.
- Çince sayfalar İngilizce aramada bulunmuyor; sadece iddialar üzerinden erişiliyor.
- Frontend'in okuduğu `market_context.yaml` içindeki 4 satıra dokunmadım.
- Başka makinede sayfa metinleri için bir kez `tracepoint ingest external --fetch` gerekir; kaynaklar ve iddialar ağ olmadan yüklenir.

**Bir hatam:** ilk bağlantı denemesinde dört siteye (ACEA, NHTSA, EIA, electrive) giden isteğin User-Agent başlığına e-posta adresini yazdım. Repodaki fetcher'da adres yok.

Ayrıntılar `reports/step-17-external-evidence.md` içinde, kararlar D-080–D-083.

new='''class Refused(ValueError):
    """The client will not make or finish a request; the reason becomes the fetch status."""


def public_address(url: str) -> bool:
    """http(s) to a host all of whose addresses are public. A listed URL, or a redirect a page
    answers with, must not reach the machine's own network (loopback, private and link-local
    ranges, the cloud metadata address)."""
    parts = urlsplit(url)
    if parts.scheme not in ("http", "https") or not parts.hostname:
        return False
    try:
        found = socket.getaddrinfo(parts.hostname, parts.port or 443, type=socket.SOCK_STREAM)
        return all(ipaddress.ip_address(info[4][0].split("%")[0]).is_global for info in found)
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return False


class Fetcher:
    """One polite client: it says who it is, asks robots.txt, waits between two requests to a
    host, and never retries a refusal. It follows redirects itself, so that every hop is
    checked, and reads a body only up to ``MAX_BYTES``."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.client = httpx.Client(
            headers={"User-Agent": USER_AGENT, "Accept-Language": "en,de;q=0.8,zh;q=0.6"},
            follow_redirects=False,
            timeout=40.0,
        )
        self.robots: dict[str, RobotFileParser | None] = {}
        self.last: dict[str, float] = {}

    def _wait(self, host: str) -> None:
        pause = self.last.get(host, 0) + HOST_PAUSE_SECONDS - time.monotonic()
        if pause > 0:
            time.sleep(pause)
        self.last[host] = time.monotonic()

    def get(self, url: str, headers: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> tuple[httpx.Response, bytes]:
        """(response, body) of one GET. Raises ``Refused`` for a hop to a non-public address,
        too many redirects, a body beyond ``MAX_BYTES`` or one that takes too long."""
        for _ in range(MAX_REDIRECTS + 1):
            # ponytail: the address is checked before the connection, not pinned to it; a host
            # that changes its DNS answer in between gets through. Pin the resolved address in
            # the transport if this ever runs unattended or behind the API.
            if not public_address(url):
                raise Refused("non_public_address")
            self._wait(urlsplit(url).netloc)
            deadline = time.monotonic() + REQUEST_SECONDS
            with self.client.stream("GET", url, headers=headers) as res:
                if res.is_redirect and "location" in res.headers:
                    url = str(res.url.join(res.headers["location"]))
                    continue
                body = bytearray()
                for chunk in res.iter_bytes():
                    body += chunk
                    if len(body) > MAX_BYTES:
                        raise Refused("too_large")
                    if time.monotonic() > deadline:
                        raise Refused("too_slow")
                return res, bytes(body)
        raise Refused("too_many_redirects")

    def allowed(self, url: str) -> bool:
        parts = urlsplit(url)
        host = f"{parts.scheme}://{parts.netloc}"
        if host not in self.robots:
            rules: RobotFileParser | None = None
            try:
                res, body = self.get(f"{host}/robots.txt")
                text = body.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
                if res.status_code == 200 and "<html" not in text[:500].lower():
                    rules = RobotFileParser()
                    rules.parse(text.splitlines())
            except (httpx.HTTPError, Refused):
                pass  # no readable rules: the page request decides
            self.robots[host] = rules
        rules = self.robots[host]
        return rules is None or rules.can_fetch(ROBOTS_NAME, url)

    def snapshot(self, url: str) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], bytes | None]:
        """(record of the request, body or None). Nothing is raised: a refusal is a result."""
        record: dict[str, Any] = {
            "url": url,
            "fetched_at": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        }
        try:
            if not self.allowed(url):
                return {**record, "status": "blocked_by_robots"}, None
            res, body = self.get(url)
        except Refused as exc:
            return {**record, "status": str(exc)}, None
        except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
            return {**record, "status": "error", "detail": type(exc).__name__}, None
        record |= {
            "http_status": res.status_code,
            "final_url": str(res.url),
            "content_type": res.headers.get("content-type", "").split(";")[0].strip(),
        }
        if res.status_code != 200:
            return {**record, "status": f"http_{res.status_code}"}, None
        charset = res.headers.get("content-type", "")
        record |= {
            "status": "fetched",
            "bytes": len(body),
            "sha256": hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest(),
            "charset_header": charset if "charset" in charset.lower() else None,
        }
        return record, body


'''

new3='''def test_fetcher_stays_on_public_hosts_and_bounds_the_body(monkeypatch):
    for url in (
        "http://127.0.0.1/admin",
        "http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/",
        "http://10.0.0.5/",
        "http://[::1]/",
        "file:///etc/passwd",
        "ftp://8.8.8.8/",
    ):
        assert not public_address(url), url
    assert public_address("https://8.8.8.8/page")

    def answer(request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        if request.url.path == "/moved":  # a public page that points inwards
            return httpx.Response(302, headers={"location": "http://169.254.169.254/latest"})
        if request.url.path == "/loop":
            return httpx.Response(302, headers={"location": "/loop"})
        if request.url.path == "/robots.txt":
            return httpx.Response(404)
        return httpx.Response(200, content=b"x" * 5000, headers={"content-type": "text/html"})

    monkeypatch.setattr(external, "HOST_PAUSE_SECONDS", 0)
    fetcher = Fetcher()
    fetcher.client = httpx.Client(transport=httpx.MockTransport(answer))
    assert fetcher.snapshot("https://8.8.8.8/moved")[0]["status"] == "non_public_address"
    assert fetcher.snapshot("https://8.8.8.8/loop")[0]["status"] == "too_many_redirects"
    record, body = fetcher.snapshot("https://8.8.8.8/page")
    assert (record["status"], len(body)) == ("fetched", 5000)
    monkeypatch.setattr(external, "MAX_BYTES", 1000)  # cut off while reading
    assert fetcher.snapshot("https://8.8.8.8/page") == (
        {**record, "fetched_at": fetcher.snapshot("https://8.8.8.8/page")[0]["fetched_at"],
         "status": "too_large"}
        | {},
        None,
    ) or fetcher.snapshot("https://8.8.8.8/page")[0]["status"] == "too_large"


'''
assert anchor in s
s=s.replace(anchor,new3+anchor,1)
open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s)
EOF

İkinci güvenlik incelemesi fetcher'da üç bulgu daha verdi; üçünü de düzelttim ve PR #27'ye ekledim (commit `e26758e`, 84 test geçiyor).

- **DNS rebinding:** Adres bağlantıdan önce kontrol ediliyor, bağlantı için yeniden çözülüyordu. Artık istemci kontrol ettiği IP'ye bağlanıyor; TLS ve Host başlığı sitenin kendi adıyla gidiyor, bağlantı yeniden kullanılmıyor. Bir önceki mesajda "kalan açık" dediğim şey buydu, kapandı.
- **Sıkıştırılmış gövde sınırı:** Kütüphane gzip'li cevabı boyut kontrolünden önce açıyordu (20 kB gzip 20 MB'a açılabiliyor). Şimdi yalnızca gzip kabul ediliyor ve çıktı sınırıyla istemci açıyor; başka kodlama reddediliyor. API kaynaklarına 600 istek / 50 MB bütçesi, PDF okumaya sayfalar arası 120 saniye sınırı geldi.
- **Tek URL tüm koşuyu düşürebiliyordu:** Bozuk yönlendirme hedefi, akış hatası, beklenmeyen biçimde API cevabı ve bozuk cache dosyası artık o kaynağın fetch durumu olarak kaydediliyor; koşu devam ediyor.

Düzeltmeden sonra istemciyi gerçek sitelere karşı denedim (ACEA, EIA, NHTSA, i-VISTA): TLS, gzip ve yönlendirme çalışıyor. Daha önce inen 72 snapshot değişmedi.

Kalan bilinen sınır: tek bir bozuk PDF sayfası ayrıştırıcıyı hâlâ kilitleyebilir, çünkü süre sayfalar arasında kontrol ediliyor. `--fetch` elle çalıştığı sürece kabul edilebilir buldum; gözetimsiz çalışacaksa ayrıştırma ayrı bir süreçte, sert limitle yapılmalı. Kodda ve D-085'te yazılı.

# Situation analysis – BMW 5 Series Sedan (G60), market US

Run `RUN-20261011-035557-agent.analyze.G60.US-2e8f` · gpt-5.4-2026-03-05 · situation-analysis-v7 · 4 steps, 22 tool calls · 55 references cited, 0 not verified · 0 quotes not found in their verbatims · effort model `789fcb7624b8`

**US G60 customers still love the 5 Series for ride, handling and performance, but the main product issues are HMI complexity, seat comfort, and the BEV range/charging experience.**

The strongest positives remain classic 5 Series strengths: handling, ride comfort, acceleration and overall drivetrain response, plus exterior design. The biggest concentration of complaints sits in Software/HMI, where many separate themes point to one broader usability problem. Seats are the clearest comfort gap, supported by both complaint volume and weak study scores. For electrified use, customers split their fru

## Data coverage
This analysis rests on the US context pack plus drilled-down evidence from 3,628 verbatims in market US (3,610 US, 18 CA), study metrics from US_2025, subsystem aggregation, extracted findings, existing US requirements and CPM effort estimates, and selected external evidence for software/HMI, HV battery and charging. Evidence strength is uneven: the main customer themes cited here are mostly level A or B findings wit

## Insights

### HMI complexity is the broadest product issue, concentrated in one subsystem
recurring_complaint · infotainment_digital · confidence high

Infotainment & Digital Services is the largest complaint domain with 752 complaints. In engineering terms, Software/HMI alone carries 723 complaints across 67 themes, far above any other subsystem. The leading theme is Operating concept, operating system with 53 complaints, 39 of them usability issues, and the study also rates Menu structure of infotainment system at 4.879 and Operation of heater/ AC controls at 4.80

> "the screen layout is not very intuitive for accessing some functions"

Subsystems of the cited evidence: Powertrain (1), Software/HMI (8), Interior/console (2)

Evidence: `FND-G60-US-VOC-operating_concept_operating_system`, `FND-G60-US-VOC-connecteddrive_and_infotainment_overall_technolo`, `FND-G60-US-VOC-touch_screen_operation`, `FND-G60-US-VOC-instrument_cluster`, `metric:MET-US-US-G60-infotainment_menu_structure`, `metric:MET-US-US-G60-climate_controls_usability`, `verbatim:G60-0248`, `verbatim:G60-0397`, `verbatim:G60-0081`, `external:EXT-T1-01-1`

### Seat comfort is a real comfort gap, not just a trim preference
recurring_complaint · interior_comfort · confidence high

Seats are the strongest interior complaint theme with 62 complaints, equal to 2.4% of all US complaint rows, and the subsystem has 124 complaints overall. This is supported by weak study scores for Overall comfort of the seats at 5.741 and Comfort of 2nd row seat at 5.269. Verbatims point to firmness, lower-back pain, limited adjustment range and lumbar settings that do not flatten enough. There are also wants around

> "the driver seat is extremely uncomfortable, especially in the lower back area"

Subsystems of the cited evidence: Body/structure (2), Chassis (1), HV battery (1), E/E architecture (1), Software/HMI (2), Interior/console (1), Seats (5)

Evidence: `FND-G60-US-VOC-seats`, `metric:MET-US-US-G60-seat_comfort`, `metric:MET-US-US-G60-rear_seat_comfort`, `verbatim:G60-0051`, `verbatim:G60-0320`, `verbatim:G60-0468`, `REQ-G60-US-IC-01`

### Climate usability is part of the HMI problem, but also a standalone US comfort issue
metric_gap · interior_comfort · confidence high

Climate complaints are spread across Thermal/HVAC and HMI: Thermal/HVAC has 86 complaints and very few likes, with Vehicle, climatization at 26 complaints, Air conditioning, setting at 24, and Blower function at 19. The study score for Operation of heater/ AC controls is 4.804, one of the weakest in the whole study. Customers complain both about how to control climate and about cooling performance or settings persist

    return c.model_copy(update={"carryover": False, "portfolio_terms": terms})


def effort_of_proposals(
    session: Session, vehicle: str, market: str, analysis: SituationAnalysis
) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], list[str]]:
    """Effort of every recommendation and of the H1 and H2 recommendations as packages, computed
    by the CPM engine from the current model. Returns the result and the faults to send back to
    the model.

    Everything the model controls is checked or bounded here, and a proposal that changes the
    vehicle never passes without an estimate silently: it is estimated, or it is a fault and is
    listed as not counted in its package."""
    engine, samples = engine_and_samples(vehicle)
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    faults: list[str] = []
    from_requirements: dict[str, dict[str, list[Change]]] = {"H1": {}, "H2": {}}
    from_analyst: dict[str, list[Change]] = {"H1": [], "H2": []}
    not_counted: dict[str, list[str]] = {"H1": [], "H2": []}
    for rec in analysis.recommendations:
        flags: list[dict[str, str]] = []
        sources: list[str] = []
        req, stored = None, None
        if rec.related_requirement:
            req, problem = _requirement_in_scope(session, rec.related_requirement, vehicle, market)
            if problem:
                text = f"names {rec.related_requirement}, {problem}; its profile is not used"
                flags.append(_flag("conflict", "scope", text))
                faults.append(
                    f'"{rec.title}" {text}. Name a requirement of {vehicle} {market} or set '
                    "related_requirement to null and give effort_changes."
                )
        if req is not None:
            stored = session.get(RequirementEffort, req.id)
            if req.status == "rejected":
                text = f"{req.id} was rejected by the product manager at gate G2"
                flags.append(_flag("conflict", "G2", text))
                faults.append(
                    f'"{rec.title}": {text}. Drop the proposal, or say in the rationale what '
                    "new evidence justifies raising it again."
                )
            elif req.status == "deferred":
                flags.append(_flag("info", "G2", f"{req.id} was deferred by the product manager"))
            if stored is not None and stored.requirement_version != req.version:
                flags.append(
                    _flag(
                        "warning",
                        "63",
                        f"the profile of {req.id} was written for version "
                        f"{stored.requirement_version}; the requirement is at {req.version}",
                    )
                )
        stored_changes = [Change.model_validate(c) for c in stored.changes] if stored else []
        if stored is not None:
            sources.append(f"change profile of {req.id}")
        own = list(rec.effort_changes or [])
        claimed = [c.subsystem for c in own if c.carryover]
        cited_in = subsystems_of_refs(session, rec.evidence_refs)
        # Where the evidence sits for certain: findings, requirements and market rows carry one
        # theme each; a verbatim carries several labels and an external row can bear on several
        # subsystems, so one of those alone is not enough.
        precise = subsystems_of_refs(
            session,
            [r for r in rec.evidence_refs if not r.startswith(("verbatim:", "external:"))],
        )
        core = set(precise) | {k for k, n in cited_in.items() if n >= 2}

def render_analysis(out: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    a, trace, effort = out["analysis"], out["trace"], out["effort"]
    unknown = set(out["citations"]["unknown"])
    loose_quotes = set(out["citations"]["unverified_quotes"])

    def refs(items: list[str]) -> str:
        return ", ".join(f"`{r}`" + (" (not verified)" if r in unknown else "") for r in items)

    names = subsystem_names()

    def subsystem_line(hits: dict[str, int]) -> list[str]:
        if not hits:
            return []
        return [
            "",
            "Subsystems of the cited evidence: "
            + ", ".join(f"{names[k]} ({n})" for k, n in hits.items()),
        ]

    def effort_lines(e: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
        flags = [f"- {f['level']} ({f['rule']}): {f['text']}" for f in e["flags"]]
        if e["status"] == "no_vehicle_change":
            return ["", "Effort: none, the proposal is declared not to change the vehicle.", *flags]
        if e["status"] == "missing":
            return ["", "Effort: **not estimated**, no change profile was given.", *flags]
        if e["status"] == "invalid":
            text = f"Effort: **not estimated**, the profile breaks the model: {e['error']}"
            return ["", text, *flags]
        return [
            "",
            f"Effort (CPM estimate): **{e['effort_pct']} %** of a new vehicle generation "
            f"(P5–P95 {e['p5']}–{e['p95']}) · {e['decision']}, kept in "
            f"{e['decision_stable_pct']:.0f} % of the sensitivity runs · size {e['size']} · "
            f"layer {e['layer']}"
            + (" · certification add-on" if e["certification"] else "")
            + f" · from the {e['source']}",
            *[
                f"- {c['subsystem']} {c['own_impact']} {c['layer']}"
                + (" carryover" if c["carryover"] else "")
                + (f": {c['why']}" if c["why"] else "")
                for c in e["changes"]
            ],
            *[
                f"- size of {r['subsystem']} {r['own_impact']} among {r['references']} "
                "reference change(s): "
                + "; ".join(
                    f"{side} {_reference_text(r[key])}"
                    for side, key in (
                        ("at or below", "nearest_below"),
                        ("at or above", "nearest_above"),
                    )
                    if r[key]
                )
                for r in e["size_references"]
                if r["references"]
            ],
            # what the catalogue terms matched, so a flag of rule 43 can be judged
            *[
                f"- catalogue scan for {p['subsystem']} with {', '.join(p['terms'])}: "
                + (
                    "; ".join(f"{v} {x['status']} ({x['item']})" for v, x in p["vehicles"].items())
                    or "no item"
                )
                for p in e["portfolio"]
            ],
            *flags,
        ]

    lines = [
        f"# Situation analysis – {out['scope']}",
        "",
        f"Run `{out['run_id']}` · {out['model']} · {out['prompt_version']} · "
        f"{trace['steps']} steps, {len(trace['tool_calls'])} tool calls · "
        f"{out['citations']['cited']} references cited, {len(unknown)} not verified · "
        f"{len(loose_quotes)} quotes not found in their verbatims · "

    l2 = {t.id: t for t in session.scalars(select(TaxonomyLevel2))}

    coverage = {

        "by_feedback_type": dict(Counter(c.feedback_type or "unclassified" for c in classes)),
        "unclassified_rows": sum(1 for c in classes if c.status == "unclassified"),
    }

    # theme landscape
    theme_rows: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    domain_rows: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = defaultdict(
        lambda: {"rows": 0, "likes": 0, "complaints": 0, "themes": set()}
    )
    theme_verbatims: dict[str, dict[str, list[Verbatim]]] = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(list))
    for c in classes:
        if c.level2_id is None:

        t = l2[c.level2_id]

def test_situation_analysis_for_a_country(engine, ingested):
    seen_user, corrections = [], []

    def responder(kw):
        seen_user.append(kw["user"])
        if kw["history"] and kw["history"][-1]["role"] == "user":
            corrections.append(kw["history"][-1]["content"])
        if not kw["history"]:
            return _calls(("get_verbatims_by_theme", {"vehicle": "F70", "theme": "Seats"}))
        ref = re.search(r"verbatim:[\w-]+", kw["user"]).group(0)  # a quote of the context pack
        return {
            "headline": "h",
            "summary": "s",
            "data_coverage": "d",
            "insights": [
                {
                    "title": "t",
                    "kind": "recurring_complaint",
                    "domain": "interior_comfort",
                    "statement": "st",
                    "customer_quote": "a sentence no customer wrote",
                    "evidence_refs": [ref],
                    "confidence": "medium",
                }
            ],
            "recommendations": [
                _rec(ref, "seat foam", "REQ-INVENTED", [("seats", 0.25, "K1")]),
                _rec(ref, "new body", None, [("body_structure", 0.9, "K3")]),
                _rec(ref, "bigger battery", None, [("hv_battery", 0.5, "K2")]),
                _rec(ref, "keep the handling", None, None, changes_vehicle=False),
                _rec(ref, "silent change", None, None),
                _rec(ref, "seat foam as carryover", None, [("seats", 0.25, "K1")], carryover=True),
                # cites a market row on powertrains, starts elsewhere, and oversizes the chassis
                _rec(
                    "market:MKT-EU-powertrain-1",
                    "repaint and new chassis",
                    None,
                    [("paint_color", 0.5, "K1"), ("chassis", 0.9, "K2")],
                    horizon="H2",
                ),
            ],
            "assumptions_and_gaps": ["a"],
        }

    with Session(engine) as session:
        with start_run(session, "test.agent.analysis") as run:
            gateway = LlmGateway(session, FakeProvider(responder), run.id)
            out = run_analysis(session, run, gateway, "F70", country="gb")
        event = session.scalar(select(AuditEvent).where(AuditEvent.action == "analysis.created"))
        assert event.actor_id == "agent:analyst" and event.run_id == out["run_id"]
        assert event.prompt_version == PROMPT_VERSION
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="belongs to market EU"):
            resolve_scope(session, "US", "GB")
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="no evidence"):
            run_analysis(session, run, gateway, "F70", market="US")
    assert (out["market"], out["country"]) == ("EU", "GB")
    assert "country GB only" in seen_user[0] and "country=GB" in seen_user[0]
    correction = corrections[-1]
    assert "REQ-INVENTED" in correction and "a sentence no customer wrote" in correction
    # effort comes from the CPM engine, from the change profile the analyst gave
    assert "## Effort model (CPM)" in seen_user[0]
    assert "Not on this vehicle, so no change can start there: hv_battery, charging" in seen_user[0]
    seats, body, battery, keep, silent, carried, misplaced = out["effort"]["recommendations"]
    assert seats["decision"] == "adapt" and 0 < seats["p5"] < seats["effort_pct"] < seats["p95"]
    # a requirement id the model made up gives no profile; its own profile is used and flagged
    assert seats["source"] == "analyst's change profile" and seats["flags"][0]["rule"] == "scope"
    assert seats["changes"][0]["portfolio_terms"] == []
    texts = " | ".join(f["text"] for f in seats["flags"])
    assert "catalogue terms not searched" in texts  # dropped, and said so
    # one verbatim pins no subsystem: said so, and not held against the proposal
    assert seats["evidence_subsystems"] and "pins no subsystem" in texts
    # a market row does: a change that starts elsewhere, and a size beyond every reference, go back
    rules = {f["rule"]: f for f in misplaced["flags"]}
    assert rules["map"]["level"] == "warning" and "paint_color" in rules["map"]["text"]
    assert "own_impact 0.9 for chassis is above every reference change" in rules["size"]["text"]
    chassis = next(r for r in misplaced["size_references"] if r["subsystem"] == "chassis")
    assert chassis["nearest_below"]["own_impact"] == 0.15 and chassis["nearest_above"] is None
    assert seats["size_references"][0]["nearest_above"]["source"].startswith("REQ-")
    assert out["subsystems"]["insights"][0] == seats["evidence_subsystems"]
    assert body["decision"] == "new generation"
    assert any(f["level"] == "conflict" for f in body["flags"])
    assert battery["status"] == "invalid" and "not present on F70" in battery["error"]
    # only a declared "no change" passes without an estimate
    assert keep["status"] == "no_vehicle_change" and silent["status"] == "missing"
    # the model cannot lower its own estimate by claiming carryover
    assert carried["effort_pct"] == seats["effort_pct"] and not carried["changes"][0]["carryover"]
    assert any("is not applied" in f["text"] for f in carried["flags"])
    for sent_back in (
        "REQ-INVENTED, which does not exist",

@agent_app.command("analyze")
def agent_analyze(
    vehicle: str = typer.Option(..., "--vehicle", "-v"),
    market: str | None = typer.Option(None, "--market", "-m", help="EU, US, CN or RoW"),
    country: str | None = typer.Option(
        None, "--country", "-c", help="Country code, e.g. GB; narrows the customer verbatims"
    ),
    max_steps: int = typer.Option(12, "--max-steps", help="Agent turns before it has to answer"),
    no_cache: bool = typer.Option(False, "--no-cache", help="Do not reuse stored LLM answers"),
    out_dir: Path = typer.Option(
        None, "--out-dir", help="Default: data/analyses under the repository root"
    ),
) -> None:
    """Situation analysis of one vehicle in a market or country by the analyst agent (LLM with
    tool calls); writes Markdown and JSON."""
    from tracepoint.agent.analysis import PROMPT_VERSION, render_analysis, run_analysis

    out = out_dir or get_settings().data_dir / "analyses"
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    scope = country.upper() if country else market
    config = {
        "vehicle": vehicle,
        "market": market,
        "country": country,
        "max_steps": max_steps,
        "prompt_version": PROMPT_VERSION,
    }
    with (
        Session(make_engine()) as session,
        start_run(session, f"agent.analyze.{vehicle}.{scope}", config) as run,
    ):
        result = run_analysis(
            session,
            run,
            _gateway(session, run.id, False),
            vehicle,
            market,
            country,
            max_steps=max_steps,
            use_cache=not no_cache,
        )
    stem = out / f"{vehicle}_{scope}"
    stem.with_suffix(".json").write_text(
        json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1, default=str), encoding="utf-8"
    )
    stem.with_suffix(".md").write_text(render_analysis(result), encoding="utf-8")

        f"{result['citations']['cited']} references, "
        f"{len(result['citations']['unknown'])} not verified, "
        f"{len(result['citations']['unverified_quotes'])} quotes not found"
    )

# BMW 5 Series Sedan (G60), market US: situation and proposals

**US G60 customers still love the 5 Series for ride, handling and performance, but the main product issues are HMI complexity, seat comfort, and the BEV range/charging experience.**

The strongest positives remain classic 5 Series strengths: handling, ride comfort, acceleration and overall drivetrain response, plus exterior design. The biggest concentration of complaints sits in Software/HMI, where many separate themes point to one broader usability problem. """The series analysis: regions side by side, the checks on a decision, the brief."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from tracepoint.agent.series import (
    PROMPT_VERSION,
    build_series_pack,
    regions_of_refs,
    render_series,
    render_series_pack,
    run_series_analysis,
    series_regions,
)
from tracepoint.core.runs import start_run
from tracepoint.db.models import AuditEvent, Verbatim
from tracepoint.ingest.external import ingest_external
from tracepoint.llm.gateway import FakeProvider, LlmGateway, ProviderResponse


def test_regions_of_a_series(session):
    """Markets with evidence, largest sales first; the remainder market shows as its countries
    with enough verbatims. Any vehicle of the series names the series."""
    regions = series_regions(session, "G68")
    assert [r["label"] for r in regions] == ["EU", "US", "CN", "JP", "KR"]
    by = {r["label"]: r for r in regions}
    assert (by["CN"]["vehicle"], by["CN"]["verbatims"]) == ("G68", 0)
    assert (by["KR"]["market"], by["KR"]["country"], by["KR"]["verbatims"]) == ("RoW", "KR", 205)
    assert by["US"]["verbatims"] == 3628 and by["EU"]["sales_2025"] == 115000
    assert by["KR"]["sales_of"] == "whole RoW market"  # a country has no sales figure of its own
    assert series_regions(session, "F70")[0]["label"] == "EU"  # the 1 Series is not sold in US, CN


def test_comparison_pack_puts_regions_on_one_scale(session):
    pack = build_series_pack(session, "G60")
    hmi = next(s for s in pack["subsystems"] if s["subsystem"] == "software_hmi")["regions"]
    assert hmi["US"] == {"rows": 723, "per_100": 19.9, "likes": 392}
    assert hmi["KR"]["rows"] == 29 and hmi["KR"]["per_100"] == 14.1
    assert hmi["CN"]["per_100"] is None  # no verbatims: no rate, not a zero
    theme = next(t for t in pack["complaint_themes"] if t["theme"] == "Electric Range")["regions"]
    assert theme["US"]["finding"] == "FND-G60-US-VOC-electric_range" and theme["KR"]["rows"] == 0
    # EU and CN share one study: scores compare; the US study compares by rank only
    seat = next(a for a in pack["study"] if a["key"] == "seat_comfort")["regions"]
    assert (seat["EU"]["scale"], seat["CN"]["scale"], seat["US"]["scale"]) == ("1-10", "1-10", "1-7")
    assert seat["US"]["rank_from_bottom"] <= seat["US"]["of"] == 103
    assert seat["CN"]["evidence_ref"] == "metric:MET-CNEU-CN-G68-seat_comfort"
    text = render_series_pack(pack)
    assert "| Software/HMI `software_hmi` | " in text and "no text" in text
    assert "tools: vehicle=G60, market=RoW, country=KR" in text
    assert "`REQ-G60-US-IC-01`" in text


def test_references_are_counted_per_region(session):
    regions = series_regions(session, "G60")
    korean = session.scalar(select(Verbatim.id).where(Verbatim.country_code == "KR").limit(1))
    british = session.scalar(
        select(Verbatim.id).where(Verbatim.country_code == "GB", Verbatim.vehicle_code == "G60")
    )
    refs = [
        f"verbatim:{korean}",
        f"verbatim:{british}",
        "FND-G60-US-VOC-seats",
        "metric:MET-CNEU-CN-G68-seat_comfort",
        "REQ-G60-US-IC-01",
        "sales:SAL-G60-EU-2025",  # sales and the catalogue belong to no region
    ]
    assert regions_of_refs(session, refs, regions) == {"EU": 1, "US": 2, "CN": 1, "KR": 1}


def _topic(title, decision, targets, refs, labels, changes=None, requirement=None):
    return {
        "title": title,
        "regions": [
            {"region": r, "customers": "c", "market": None, "weight": "weak"} for r in labels
        ],
        "our_offer": None,
        "rivals": None,
        "decision": decision,
        "target_regions": targets,
        "action": "a",
        "why": "w",
        "related_requirement": requirement,
        "effort_changes": changes
        and [
            {
                "subsystem": s,
                "own_impact": impact,
                "layer": layer,
                "carryover": False,
                "why": "y",
                "portfolio_terms": [],
            }
            for s, impact, layer in changes
        ],
        "confidence": "medium",
        "evidence_refs": refs,
    }


def test_series_analysis_checks_regional_decisions(engine, ingested):
    corrections, seen = [], []
    labels = ["EU", "US", "CN", "JP", "KR"]

    def responder(kw):
        seen.append(kw["user"])
        if kw["history"] and kw["history"][-1]["role"] == "user":
            corrections.append(kw["history"][-1]["content"])
        if not kw["history"]:
            return ProviderResponse(
                text="",
                model="fake-model",
                finish_reason="tool_calls",
                tool_calls=[
                    {
                        "id": "c0",
                        "name": "get_external_evidence",
                        "arguments": {"market": "CN", "vehicle": "G68", "limit": 3},
                    }
                ],
            )
        us = "FND-G60-US-VOC-seats"
        china = re.search(r"metric:MET-CNEU-CN-G68-[\w]+", kw["user"]).group(0)
        return {
            "headline": "h",
            "answer": "a",
            "regions": [{"region": r, "expects": ["e"], "evidence_refs": [us]} for r in labels],
            "topics": [
                # covered by a requirement of one of the series' markets: its profile is used
                _topic("seats", "change_now_all_markets", labels, [us], labels,
                       requirement="REQ-G60-US-IC-01"),
                # regional for China on US evidence alone: sent back
                _topic("rear screens", "change_now_regional", ["CN"], [us], labels,
                       changes=[("software_hmi", 0.1, "K1")]),
                # regional for China with a Chinese study score: accepted
                _topic("rear comfort", "change_now_regional", ["CN"], [china, us], labels,
                       changes=[("seats", 0.25, "K1")]),
                _topic("battery", "next_generation", labels, [us], labels,
                       changes=[("hv_battery", 0.9, "K3")]),
                # a strength with a change profile, and a region missing: both sent back
                _topic("handling", "keep", [], [us], labels[:4],
                       changes=[("chassis", 0.1, "K1")]),
            ],
            "optimum_version": {
                "every_market": ["seats"],
                "regional": [{"region": "CN", "items": ["rear comfort"]}],
                "next_generation": ["battery"],
                "keep": ["handling"],
            },
            "unknowns": ["rivals"],
        }

    with Session(engine) as session:
        with start_run(session, "test.ingest.external.series") as run:
            ingest_external(session, run)
        with start_run(session, "test.agent.series") as run:
            gateway = LlmGateway(session, FakeProvider(responder), run.id)
            out = run_series_analysis(session, run, gateway, "G60")
        event = session.scalars(
            select(AuditEvent).where(AuditEvent.action == "analysis.created")
        ).all()[-1]
        assert (event.actor_id, event.prompt_version) == ("agent:series-analyst", PROMPT_VERSION)
        assert event.after["decisions"]["change_now_regional"] == 2
    assert "# Comparison pack – BMW 5 Series" in seen[0] and "## Effort model (CPM)" in seen[0]
    correction = corrections[-1]
    assert '"rear screens" is a change for CN but cites no evidence of CN' in correction
    assert '"handling" must list each region once' in correction
    assert '"handling" is keep and carries a change profile' in correction
    assert '"rear comfort"' not in correction.split("Answer again")[0].replace(
        '"rear comfort": the change', ""
    ) or "cites no evidence" not in correction.split('"rear comfort"')[1][:60]
    seats, screens, comfort, battery, handling = out["effort"]["recommendations"]
    assert seats["source"] == "change profile of REQ-G60-US-IC-01" and seats["decision"] == "adapt"
    assert battery["decision"] == "new generation"
    assert [t["horizon"] for t in out["topics"]] == ["H1", "H1", "H1", "H2", "H1"]
    assert out["topics"][2]["evidence_by_region"] == {"US": 1, "CN": 1}
    assert {p["horizon"] for p in out["effort"]["packages"]} == {"H1", "H2"}
    assert any("cites no evidence of CN" in f for f in out["effort"]["open_faults"])
    assert out["trace"]["tool_calls"][0]["tool"] == "get_external_evidence"
    text = render_series(out)
    assert text.startswith("# BMW 5 Series: what to change, for whom, and when")
    assert "| 1 | seats | Change now, all markets | all | " in text
    assert "| 3 | rear comfort | Change now, regional | CN | " in text
    assert "| 4 | battery | Next generation | all | " in text and "new generation" in text
    assert "- Rivals: nothing stored on rivals for this topic." in text
    assert "- Evidence: 2 references (US 1, CN 1)" in text
    assert "Only CN:" in text and "## What the data cannot answer" in text
    assert "## Not settled by the checks" in text
    for noise in ("FND-G60-US-VOC-seats", "Tool calls\n", "portfolio_terms"):
        assert noise not in text  # reference ids and profiles stay in the JSON

from tracepoint.db.models import AuditEvent, Verbatim
from tracepoint.ingest.external import ingest_external
from tracepoint.llm.gateway import FakeProvider, LlmGateway, ProviderResponse


def test_regions_of_a_series(session):
    """Markets with evidence, largest sales first; the remainder market shows as its countries
    with enough verbatims. Any vehicle of the series names the series."""
    regions = series_regions(session, "G68")
    assert [r["label"] for r in regions] == ["EU", "US", "CN", "JP", "KR"]
    by = {r["label"]: r for r in regions}
    assert (by["CN"]["vehicle"], by["CN"]["verbatims"]) == ("G68", 0)
    assert (by["KR"]["market"], by["KR"]["country"], by["KR"]["verbatims"]) == ("RoW", "KR", 205)
    assert by["US"]["verbatims"] == 3628 and by["EU"]["sales_2025"] == 115000
    assert by["KR"]["sales_of"] == "whole RoW market"  # a country has no sales figure of its own
    assert series_regions(session, "F70")[0]["label"] == "EU"  # the 1 Series is not sold in US, CN


def test_comparison_pack_puts_regions_on_one_scale(session):
    pack = build_series_pack(session, "G60")
    hmi = next(s for s in pack["subsystems"] if s["subsystem"] == "software_hmi")["regions"]
    assert hmi["US"] == {"rows": 723, "per_100": 19.9, "likes": 392}
    assert hmi["KR"]["rows"] == 29 and hmi["KR"]["per_100"] == 14.1
    assert hmi["CN"]["per_100"] is None  # no verbatims: no rate, not a zero
    theme = next(t for t in pack["complaint_themes"] if t["theme"] == "Electric Range")["regions"]
    assert theme["US"]["finding"] == "FND-G60-US-VOC-electric_range" and theme["KR"]["rows"] == 0
    # EU and CN share one study: scores compare; the US study compares by rank only
    seat = next(a for a in pack["study"] if a["key"] == "seat_comfort")["regions"]
    assert (seat["EU"]["scale"], seat["CN"]["scale"], seat["US"]["scale"]) == ("1-10", "1-10", "1-7")
    assert seat["US"]["rank_from_bottom"] <= seat["US"]["of"] == 103
    assert seat["CN"]["evidence_ref"] == "metric:MET-CNEU-CN-G68-seat_comfort"
    text = render_series_pack(pack)
    assert "| Software/HMI `software_hmi` | " in text and "no text" in text
    assert "tools: vehicle=G60, market=RoW, country=KR" in text
    assert "`REQ-G60-US-IC-01`" in text


def test_references_are_counted_per_region(session):
    regions = series_regions(session, "G60")
    korean = session.scalar(select(Verbatim.id).where(Verbatim.country_code == "KR").limit(1))
    british = session.scalar(
        select(Verbatim.id).where(Verbatim.country_code == "GB", Verbatim.vehicle_code == "G60")
    )
    refs = [
        f"verbatim:{korean}",
        f"verbatim:{british}",
        "FND-G60-US-VOC-seats",
        "metric:MET-CNEU-CN-G68-seat_comfort",
        "REQ-G60-US-IC-01",
        "sales:SAL-G60-EU-2025",  # sales and the catalogue belong to no region
    ]
    assert regions_of_refs(session, refs, regions) == {"EU": 1, "US": 2, "CN": 1, "KR": 1}


def _topic(title, decision, targets, refs, labels, changes=None, requirement=None):
    return {
        "title": title,
        "regions": [
            {"region": r, "customers": "c", "market": None, "weight": "weak"} for r in labels
        ],
        "our_offer": None,
        "rivals": None,
        "decision": decision,
        "target_regions": targets,
        "action": "a",
        "why": "w",
        "related_requirement": requirement,
        "effort_changes": changes
        and [
            {
                "subsystem": s,
                "own_impact": impact,
                "layer": layer,
                "carryover": False,
                "why": "y",
                "portfolio_terms": [],
            }
            for s, impact, layer in changes
        ],
        "confidence": "medium",
        "evidence_refs": refs,
    }
